title: Celebrating the Arts: Fourth Fridays!
venue: Seminole County Convention and Visitors Bureau
description:
In the heart of Central Florida, Seminole County is quickly becoming a favorite destination. Whether you're looking for a newer hotel, at a better rate, the enjoyment of the natural wonders of a true Florida vacation, fine dining, miles of crystal clear rivers and wilderness trails, superb golf courses or simply to relax your mind and soul in our charming historic villages - it's easy to see why Seminole County is Florida's Natural Choice.

Located between the theme parks of Central Florida and the beautiful Treasure Coast beaches, access to Seminole County is a breeze. Whether visitors fly into hassle-free Sanford-Orlando International Airport or Orlando International, or arrive by Amtrak or by vehicle on I-4, the excitement is only a short hop away.

Visitors find many of the same flagship hotels and amenities as in Orlando, but often for a significantly lower rate. In addition to the excellent hotels that our guests currently enjoy, Seminole County has recently opened new hotels including a Hyatt Place, Residence Inn and a Westin.

Seminole County boasts 2,000 freshwater lakes and clear running rivers that create an abundance of outdoor activities. From kayaking to fishing, boating and hiking, the Wekiva River, Wekiva Springs State Park and other areas have become popular attractions. Showing a wilder side, flat-bottom airboats propel riders on an exhilarating trip in search of alligators and wildlife. A great new attraction located at the Central Florida Zoo and Botanical Gardens is ZOOm Air Adventures - an aerial adventure course that allows visitors to explore the tree tops from an animal's perspective. The only course of its kind in the United States, ZOOm Air is completely environmentally friendly and goes well beyond the usual zip line courses. For the less adventurous, the 1940's style Rivership Romance hosts luncheon and moonlight dinner cruises on the tranquil St. Johns River. Alternatively, the area hosts several golf courses, great antique shopping and charming villages with restaurants and nightlife for every taste.

Surrounded by the beauty of natural Florida, Seminole County offers the classic Florida experience.

title: Free Lecture Series
description:
The Florida Carriage Museum & Resort encompasses over 400 acres of beauty in Central Florida’s horse country. Visitors to the Museum re-live history as they experience one of the finest collections of carriages in the world. They can even take a carriage ride (by prior appointment) on the winding roads through tall oaks draped in Spanish Moss, around the Qin Dynasty Gardens and past the exotic Japanese Koi Pond. Horses abound: a rare Poitou donkey named “Nicolette” and her best friend, a Miniature Horse named “Gracie”, welcome visitors and look for a scratch on the head.

The Museum houses one of the largest, privately owned collections of carriages in the world. It is open to the public and there are more than 160 meticulously restored carriages, including the 1840’s Dress Chariot formerly owned by Emperor Franz Joseph of Austria.

The Resort features 24 well appointed residences and 10 barns that serve as an equine “Bed & Barn.” Some guests bring their horses to train for the winter months, a weekend, or just for the day. Others come without horses to enjoy the miles of walking/carriage trails and can often be spotted picnicing under the shady oak trees.

Amelia Island is synonymous for its protected wildlife, state parks and family-filled adventure. title: History of Fort Mose
address: 15 Fort Mose Trl., off of U.S. 1 North
description: The first free African settlement in North America and a premier site on the Florida Black Heritage trail. In 1738, the Spanish governor of Florida chartered Fort Mose as a settlement for freed Africans who had fled slavery in the British Carolinas. When Spain ceded Florida to Britain in 1763, the inhabitants of Fort Mose migrated to Cuba. Although nothing remains of the fort, the site was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1994 for its importance in American history.

title: How, When & Where To Find Shells Workshop
description:
Sanibel & Captiva are considered the shelling capital of North America. More than 300 species of shells can be found in the shallow water surrounding the islands.

The Bailey-Matthews Shell Museum is the only museum in the country dedicated entirely to shells. Over thirty exhibits tell the story of mollusks from around the world. Exhibits are devoted to shells in art and history, shell habitats, rare specimens, fossil shells and common Southwest Florida shells. Two live mollusk videos alternate continuously every 30 minutes.

Children are mesmerized by the children’s learning lab featuring a hands-on play area and a “live tank” with indigenous mollusks. This area provides a golden opportunity for children to experience the museum rather than merely observing exhibits. A half-hour video, Mollusks in Action, is shown on the hour and a children's video is shown continuously.

The museum is passionate about children’s education. The goal is for the museum to come alive as an exciting learning center instead of just a building.

Young girls are in awe when they discover that at one time shells were used as money and a bride’s value was calculated “in shells.” Many children stare in disbelief when learning that shells are actually made by a creature and the creature has a self propelling foot, a mouth and in the case of scallops, even eyes.

Summer Camps, Mommy and Me Play Sessions, a Youth Docent Program, half-day workshops, and a puppet theater are designed to help children discover the wonder of the world of shells. Children can even “shell-a-brate” their birthdays at the museum.

An exquisite gift shop offers a wide variety of unique shell-themed gifts including books, ceramics, clothing, toys and fine jewelry.

Open daily from 10 a.m. - 5 p.m. Thanksgiving, Christmas, New Year’s, Easter and the first Sunday in March are the only days the museum is closed. Admission is $7.00 for adults seventeen and up, $4.00 for youth five - 16 years of age and children four and under are free. Located close to “Ding” Darling National Wildlife Refuge. Call for program information or to register for classes. Visit their website for more information and a complete listing of programs and events.

title: Celebrating the Arts: Fourth Fridays!
venue: Seminole County Convention and Visitors Bureau
description:
In the heart of Central Florida, Seminole County is quickly becoming a favorite destination. Whether you're looking for a newer hotel, at a better rate, the enjoyment of the natural wonders of a true Florida vacation, fine dining, miles of crystal clear rivers and wilderness trails, superb golf courses or simply to relax your mind and soul in our charming historic villages - it's easy to see why Seminole County is Florida's Natural Choice.

Located between the theme parks of Central Florida and the beautiful Treasure Coast beaches, access to Seminole County is a breeze. Whether visitors fly into hassle-free Sanford-Orlando International Airport or Orlando International, or arrive by Amtrak or by vehicle on I-4, the excitement is only a short hop away.

Visitors find many of the same flagship hotels and amenities as in Orlando, but often for a significantly lower rate. In addition to the excellent hotels that our guests currently enjoy, Seminole County has recently opened new hotels including a Hyatt Place, Residence Inn and a Westin.

Seminole County boasts 2,000 freshwater lakes and clear running rivers that create an abundance of outdoor activities. From kayaking to fishing, boating and hiking, the Wekiva River, Wekiva Springs State Park and other areas have become popular attractions. Showing a wilder side, flat-bottom airboats propel riders on an exhilarating trip in search of alligators and wildlife. A great new attraction located at the Central Florida Zoo and Botanical Gardens is ZOOm Air Adventures - an aerial adventure course that allows visitors to explore the tree tops from an animal's perspective. The only course of its kind in the United States, ZOOm Air is completely environmentally friendly and goes well beyond the usual zip line courses. For the less adventurous, the 1940's style Rivership Romance hosts luncheon and moonlight dinner cruises on the tranquil St. Johns River. Alternatively, the area hosts several golf courses, great antique shopping and charming villages with restaurants and nightlife for every taste.

Surrounded by the beauty of natural Florida, Seminole County offers the classic Florida experience.

title: Free Lecture Series
description:
The Florida Carriage Museum & Resort encompasses over 400 acres of beauty in Central Florida’s horse country. Visitors to the Museum re-live history as they experience one of the finest collections of carriages in the world. They can even take a carriage ride (by prior appointment) on the winding roads through tall oaks draped in Spanish Moss, around the Qin Dynasty Gardens and past the exotic Japanese Koi Pond. Horses abound: a rare Poitou donkey named “Nicolette” and her best friend, a Miniature Horse named “Gracie”, welcome visitors and look for a scratch on the head.

The Museum houses one of the largest, privately owned collections of carriages in the world. It is open to the public and there are more than 160 meticulously restored carriages, including the 1840’s Dress Chariot formerly owned by Emperor Franz Joseph of Austria.

The Resort features 24 well appointed residences and 10 barns that serve as an equine “Bed & Barn.” Some guests bring their horses to train for the winter months, a weekend, or just for the day. Others come without horses to enjoy the miles of walking/carriage trails and can often be spotted picnicing under the shady oak trees.

The High Springs Main Street program is a 501 (c) 3 non-profit under the Community Development Corporation.  The Main Street approach advocates improvements in four areas to create a positive, distinctive image for downtown:

1) Organization
2) Promotion
3) Design
4) Economic Restructuring

The Main Street approach also advocates a return to community self-reliance and emphasizes the downtown's traditional assets: personal service, local ownership, unique architecture, and sense of community. 

The Main Street Program Vision is to provide vibrant, economically-sustainable High Springs downtown district that respects and preserves its historical, small-town assets.

The Main Street Mission is to provide education, support, guidance and vision for the preservation, improvement and economic restructuring of the historical High Springs downtown district.

title: History of Fort Mose
address: 15 Fort Mose Trl., off of U.S. 1 North
description: The first free African settlement in North America and a premier site on the Florida Black Heritage trail. In 1738, the Spanish governor of Florida chartered Fort Mose as a settlement for freed Africans who had fled slavery in the British Carolinas. When Spain ceded Florida to Britain in 1763, the inhabitants of Fort Mose migrated to Cuba. Although nothing remains of the fort, the site was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1994 for its importance in American history.

Sanford, one of Central Florida’s oldest incorporated cities, is home to brick-lined streets, towering oaks, elegant storefronts and many beautiful, nineteenth century Victorian homes. The picturesque downtown, which once featured feed stores and dry good sellers,now showcases unique shops, restaurants and art galleries. Events, such as the Saturday morning Farmers Market and jazz concerts in Magnolia Square; theatrical productions at the newly renovated Wayne Densch Performing Arts Center; the annual Greater Sanford Regional Chamber of Commerce Bikefest; and the monthly Alive After 5 street parties attract visitors from all over.
Sanford sits on the South shore of Lake Monroe, which provides a waterfront backdrop

You may also launch a canoe (when the river is high enough) and fish upstream from the picnic area. Fish commonly caught are bass, brim and catfish.

Sanford, one of Central Florida’s oldest incorporated cities, is home to brick-lined streets, towering oaks, elegant storefronts and many beautiful, nineteenth century Victorian homes. title: 29th Annual Down Home Days April 16 & 17th
venue: Madison County Chamber of Commerce & Tourism
description:
Madison County is the gem of North Florida rural counties. The county features a large agricultural business base, combined with retail, medical, service and professional businesses. In addition, Madison County is the home of North Florida Community College, now celebrating 50 years of service to the community. Madison is a faith-based community offering over 100 churches for its citizens. It is home to several annual festivals including the Lee Homecoming Days (early April), Down Home Days (late April in Madison), Hickory Grove Founders Day (Oct.) and the Greenville Country Christmas (Dec.). And continuing through 2009 and 2010, Downtown Madison will be hosting the Fifth Saturday Farmers and Friends Festival each fifth Sat. during the year!
     Madison County is well known for its rolling hills and beautiful vistas and is frequently visited by nationally known bicycle organizations. The county is filled with bicycle and walking trails and with three different rivers serving as our county boundaries, canoeing, kayaking and boating opportunities abound. 
     And in Madison County, "History never had it so good!"  Madison County is blessed with dozens of structures ranging from 100 years to over 150 years old. When you visit, be sure to enjoy the Treasures of Madison County Museum located on South Range Street in Madison.
     Accommodations range from nationally known hotel chains and campgrounds to quaint, totally refurbished bed & breakfast facilities.
     Visiting Madison County, is a relaxing, comforting and educational opportunity to fall back into the 19th century. And they're proud to say that they're home to over 20,000 friendly country people and just a few old grouches!
     Madison County is conveniently located on Interstate 10, between Lake City and Tallahassee and is a good stone's throw just south of Valdosta, GA.
     Come visit Madison County.  We make new friends everyday!
     For additional information call the Madison County Chamber of Commerce & Tourism or visit their website.

title: Celebrating the Arts: Fourth Fridays!
venue: Seminole County Convention and Visitors Bureau
description:
In the heart of Central Florida, Seminole County is quickly becoming a favorite destination. Whether you're looking for a newer hotel, at a better rate, the enjoyment of the natural wonders of a true Florida vacation, fine dining, miles of crystal clear rivers and wilderness trails, superb golf courses or simply to relax your mind and soul in our charming historic villages - it's easy to see why Seminole County is Florida's Natural Choice.

Located between the theme parks of Central Florida and the beautiful Treasure Coast beaches, access to Seminole County is a breeze. Whether visitors fly into hassle-free Sanford-Orlando International Airport or Orlando International, or arrive by Amtrak or by vehicle on I-4, the excitement is only a short hop away.

Visitors find many of the same flagship hotels and amenities as in Orlando, but often for a significantly lower rate. In addition to the excellent hotels that our guests currently enjoy, Seminole County has recently opened new hotels including a Hyatt Place, Residence Inn and a Westin.

Seminole County boasts 2,000 freshwater lakes and clear running rivers that create an abundance of outdoor activities. From kayaking to fishing, boating and hiking, the Wekiva River, Wekiva Springs State Park and other areas have become popular attractions. Showing a wilder side, flat-bottom airboats propel riders on an exhilarating trip in search of alligators and wildlife. A great new attraction located at the Central Florida Zoo and Botanical Gardens is ZOOm Air Adventures - an aerial adventure course that allows visitors to explore the tree tops from an animal's perspective. The only course of its kind in the United States, ZOOm Air is completely environmentally friendly and goes well beyond the usual zip line courses. For the less adventurous, the 1940's style Rivership Romance hosts luncheon and moonlight dinner cruises on the tranquil St. Johns River. Alternatively, the area hosts several golf courses, great antique shopping and charming villages with restaurants and nightlife for every taste.

Surrounded by the beauty of natural Florida, Seminole County offers the classic Florida experience.

title: Jensen Beach Pineapple Festival
description: A unique riverfront community that is known for its genuine small-town charm and warm hospitality. The Jensen Beach, Hutchinson Island area is a top vacation destination with a perfect year-round climate, uncrowded natural beaches, great fishing, beautiful parks and a unique casual lifestyle. Commonly referred to as the "Art & Soul of Florida's Treasure Coast," Jensen Beach is a premier dining and one-of-a-kind retail destination, which includes art galleries, boutiques and a regional shopping mall. title: Celebrating the Arts: Fourth Fridays!
venue: Seminole County Convention and Visitors Bureau
description:
In the heart of Central Florida, Seminole County is quickly becoming a favorite destination. Whether you're looking for a newer hotel, at a better rate, the enjoyment of the natural wonders of a true Florida vacation, fine dining, miles of crystal clear rivers and wilderness trails, superb golf courses or simply to relax your mind and soul in our charming historic villages - it's easy to see why Seminole County is Florida's Natural Choice.

Located between the theme parks of Central Florida and the beautiful Treasure Coast beaches, access to Seminole County is a breeze. Whether visitors fly into hassle-free Sanford-Orlando International Airport or Orlando International, or arrive by Amtrak or by vehicle on I-4, the excitement is only a short hop away.

Visitors find many of the same flagship hotels and amenities as in Orlando, but often for a significantly lower rate. In addition to the excellent hotels that our guests currently enjoy, Seminole County has recently opened new hotels including a Hyatt Place, Residence Inn and a Westin.

Seminole County boasts 2,000 freshwater lakes and clear running rivers that create an abundance of outdoor activities. From kayaking to fishing, boating and hiking, the Wekiva River, Wekiva Springs State Park and other areas have become popular attractions. Showing a wilder side, flat-bottom airboats propel riders on an exhilarating trip in search of alligators and wildlife. A great new attraction located at the Central Florida Zoo and Botanical Gardens is ZOOm Air Adventures - an aerial adventure course that allows visitors to explore the tree tops from an animal's perspective. The only course of its kind in the United States, ZOOm Air is completely environmentally friendly and goes well beyond the usual zip line courses. For the less adventurous, the 1940's style Rivership Romance hosts luncheon and moonlight dinner cruises on the tranquil St. Johns River. Alternatively, the area hosts several golf courses, great antique shopping and charming villages with restaurants and nightlife for every taste.

Surrounded by the beauty of natural Florida, Seminole County offers the classic Florida experience.

title: Free Lecture Series
description:
The Florida Carriage Museum & Resort encompasses over 400 acres of beauty in Central Florida’s horse country. Visitors to the Museum re-live history as they experience one of the finest collections of carriages in the world. They can even take a carriage ride (by prior appointment) on the winding roads through tall oaks draped in Spanish Moss, around the Qin Dynasty Gardens and past the exotic Japanese Koi Pond. Horses abound: a rare Poitou donkey named “Nicolette” and her best friend, a Miniature Horse named “Gracie”, welcome visitors and look for a scratch on the head.

The Museum houses one of the largest, privately owned collections of carriages in the world. It is open to the public and there are more than 160 meticulously restored carriages, including the 1840’s Dress Chariot formerly owned by Emperor Franz Joseph of Austria.

The Resort features 24 well appointed residences and 10 barns that serve as an equine “Bed & Barn.” Some guests bring their horses to train for the winter months, a weekend, or just for the day. Others come without horses to enjoy the miles of walking/carriage trails and can often be spotted picnicing under the shady oak trees.

description:

title: Superstar Clint Holmes: Celebrating the Great Sammy Davis, Jr.
venue: Bob Lappin & the Palm Beach Pops
description:
Bob Lappin & The Palm Beach Pops

The house lights dim and the spotlight comes on as he takes his place on stage. The orchestra begins to play and it becomes apparent that Maestro Bob Lappin has orchestrated yet another exceptional evening of entertainment. The musicians and singers are energized by the repertoire and the audience is immersed in the magic of the music. For a moment in time, we are captivated by the extraordinary musicianship and passion presented on stage.
As Florida’s premier Pops orchestras, Bob Lappin & The Palm Beach Pops are devoted to preserving and performing the music of the Great American Songbook. From Gershwin to Goodman…Tin Pan Alley to Broadway…Judy Garland to Frank Sinatra…the Palm Beach Pops perform your favorites like no one else can!
The Palm Beach Pops perform 36 concerts from November through April at the Kravis Center for the Performing Arts - Dreyfoos Hall - in West Palm Beach, the Carole & Barry Kaye Peforming Arts Auditorium at Florida Atlantic University in Boca Raton and Eissey Campus Theatre at Palm Beach Community College in Palm Beach Gardens.
Bringing you the music that makes you feel inspired and alive!

title: World Ocean Day
description:
Ocean adventures await year ’round at Mote Aquarium, home to more than 100 marine species and exhibits showcasing the adjoining Mote Marine Laboratory. See freaky frogfish, huge scuttling lobsters and other denizens of Southwest Florida’s Gulf Coast, including sandbar, nurse, blacknose and bonnethead sharks. Guests can also see dolphins, manatees and sea turtles.

At our brand new exhibit, the Seahorse Conservation Laboratory, you can see graceful seahorses and their tiny young, or fry. You can learn about the threats wild seahorses face and watch Mote aquarists raise these fragile fish. Guests might even witness a little seahorse romance or spot a pregnant dad (that's right — male seahorses are the only animal dads that carry young in a belly pouch). 

At our new exhibit Sea Turtles: Ancient Survivors, visitors can learn how sea turtles outlived the dinosaurs and how these animals need our help to survive in modern times. An interactive display even lets you follow the journey of real sea turtles tagged in the wild by Mote scientists and see where they went between feeding and breeding seasons.

If you want to dive deeper into ocean fun, try our new "Breakfast at Mote" tours. These group tours allow small groups to enjoy Mote’s facilities before we open our doors to the general public. Participants can linger in front of their favorite exhibits, take unobstructed photos and even see bits of our morning routine, from fish feedings to shark tank cleanings. Your admission includes a continental breakfast and guided Aquarium tour. Ticket prices are $23 per person ($11 for Mote members). Go to www.mote.org/breakfast for more info.

When you buy a ticket to Mote Aquarium, you support world-renowned research at Mote Marine Laboratory. Visitors can glimpse our cutting-edge science and learn about the lab’s founding director, Eugenie Clark, and the research she did when the lab opened its doors in 1955. You can also see the work she and other researchers are doing at Mote today.

Mote Aquarium is open from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. 365 days a year at 1600 Ken Thompson Parkway, City Island, Sarasota. Admission prices are $17 for adults, $16 for seniors and $12 for kids ages 4-12. Mote Members and kids 3 and younger always get in free.

description:
Florida's premiere aviation attraction showcases vintage aircraft from the world’s largest private collection. General admission includes flight simulators, interactive exhibits, a tram tour of aircraft maintenance areas, restoration and backlot tours and a daily aerial demonstration - a unique opportunity to see rare aircraft in flight (weather permitting). Sight and sound immersion experiences bring you back in time to Early Flight, the trenches of WWI and even on board a B-17 in a WWII bombing mission.
 
Recent additions to Fantasy of Flight attractions include audio tours, the Fun with Flight center for families, The Tuskegee Airmen – They Dared to Fly exhibit and the multimedia tribute to the WASP (Women Airforce Service Pilots) – A Passionate Pursuit.
 
Visit the Art Deco-styled Compass Rose Diner from 11 a.m.-3 p.m. daily, or Fantasy of Flight’s Gift Shop for specialty product offerings for your favorite aviation enthusiast. Both are open to the public, with no admission fee required. Parking is free (excluding special events). Hot air balloon rides and biplane rides are available for an extra charge.

title: Alive After 5 Street Party
description:

The picturesque downtown, which once featured feed stores and dry good sellers,now showcases unique shops, restaurants and art galleries. Events, such as the Saturday morning Farmers Market and jazz concerts in Magnolia Square; theatrical productions at the newly renovated Wayne Densch Performing Arts Center; the annual Greater Sanford Regional Chamber of Commerce Bikefest; and the monthly Alive After 5 street parties attract visitors from all over.
Sanford sits on the South shore of Lake Monroe, which provides a waterfront backdrop
for walking, jogging or just enjoying the natural beauty. RiverWalk, with its gazebos and swinging benches, has 1.2 miles of pedestrian walking paths. Along the way, you can visit Veterans Memorial Park, Marina Island, the Sanford Museum and Ft. Mellon Park with its new kid park and Splash Pad. Stop for lunch at one of the lakeside or nearby downtown restaurants.

title: Celery City Cruisers Car Show
description:
Sanford, one of Central Florida’s oldest incorporated cities, is home to brick-lined streets, towering oaks, elegant storefronts and many beautiful, nineteenth century Victorian homes. The picturesque downtown, which once featured feed stores and dry good sellers,now showcases unique shops, restaurants and art galleries. Events, such as the Saturday morning Farmers Market and jazz concerts in Magnolia Square; theatrical productions at the newly renovated Wayne Densch Performing Arts Center; the annual Greater Sanford Regional Chamber of Commerce Bikefest; and the monthly Alive After 5 street parties attract visitors from all over.
Sanford sits on the South shore of Lake Monroe, which provides a waterfront backdrop

Along the way, you can visit Veterans Memorial Park, Marina Island, the Sanford Museum and Ft. Mellon Park with its new kid park and Splash Pad. Stop for lunch at one of the lakeside or nearby downtown restaurants.

title: Gator Nights Join In Tour
description:
One-of-a-kind airboat tour in the heart of the Florida Everglades. Come visit this family owned and operated classic South Florida attraction deep in the swamp. With a recent half-million dollar renovation, Sawgrass now offers two exclusive adventures, the daytime Private Tour and the nighttime Red Eye Tour! Feel the excitement and learn the history of Florida's most remarkable treasure, the Everglades. As one of the rare subtropical ecosystems, the Everglades holds spectacular mysteries.
     Renew your spirit as you glide across miles of river at speeds up to 40 mph and get up close and personal with native wildlife. This once in a lifetime adventure will create lasting memories as you discover the secrets of this untamed wilderness. Start your adventure with a 30 minute airboat tour of the Florida Everglades. Your tour will be guided by one of the experienced captains who have received extensive training.
     During the tour, you'll listen to tales of how the Seminole and panther once coexisted in this lush wilderness. Also, you'll catch a glimpse of endangered wildlife as you skim across the glassy water. Take a walk on the wild side back in time with an original dinosaur, the Florida Alligator. The reptile exhibit features dozens of species both native and exotic to Florida. Along with their friendly turtles and iguanas, you can learn about Cannibal, their 1,000-pound alligator. 
     Handlers are happy to demonstrate how these animals live and survive in the wild. Be sure to bring your camera, so you can capture the excitement of you cradling one of these majestic animals with the "Hold a Baby Alligator" experience. 
     Your adventure will include a visit to the Exotic Wildlife exhibit. Predators Unlimited is a separate organization that brings a variety of animals to the park each day to visit. They strive to educate and enlighten the public about endangered species like the Florida Panther. Playful critters abound and amaze as you can see many different animals that often include panthers, lepoards and wolves.
     While you are at Sawgrass please don't miss the "Swamp"yard Island! You and your family can interact and feed many of their animals at this exhibit.

title: How, When & Where To Find Shells Workshop
description:
Sanibel & Captiva are considered the shelling capital of North America. More than 300 species of shells can be found in the shallow water surrounding the islands.

The Bailey-Matthews Shell Museum is the only museum in the country dedicated entirely to shells. Over thirty exhibits tell the story of mollusks from around the world. Exhibits are devoted to shells in art and history, shell habitats, rare specimens, fossil shells and common Southwest Florida shells. Two live mollusk videos alternate continuously every 30 minutes.

Children are mesmerized by the children’s learning lab featuring a hands-on play area and a “live tank” with indigenous mollusks. This area provides a golden opportunity for children to experience the museum rather than merely observing exhibits. A half-hour video, Mollusks in Action, is shown on the hour and a children's video is shown continuously.

The museum is passionate about children’s education. The goal is for the museum to come alive as an exciting learning center instead of just a building.

Young girls are in awe when they discover that at one time shells were used as money and a bride’s value was calculated “in shells.” Many children stare in disbelief when learning that shells are actually made by a creature and the creature has a self propelling foot, a mouth and in the case of scallops, even eyes.

Summer Camps, Mommy and Me Play Sessions, a Youth Docent Program, half-day workshops, and a puppet theater are designed to help children discover the wonder of the world of shells. Children can even “shell-a-brate” their birthdays at the museum.

An exquisite gift shop offers a wide variety of unique shell-themed gifts including books, ceramics, clothing, toys and fine jewelry.

Open daily from 10 a.m. - 5 p.m. Thanksgiving, Christmas, New Year’s, Easter and the first Sunday in March are the only days the museum is closed. Admission is $7.00 for adults seventeen and up, $4.00 for youth five - 16 years of age and children four and under are free. Located close to “Ding” Darling National Wildlife Refuge. Call for program information or to register for classes. Visit their website for more information and a complete listing of programs and events.

title: FUNTASTIC FRIDAYS FOR KIDS
description:
Hollywood is a classic Florida beachtown that’s enchanted visitors since the 1920s. Visitors love the Hollywood Trolley which provides a scenic way to enjoy the best of Hollywood Beach and Downtown. Hollywood Beach features a one-of-a-kind oceanfront promenade called the Hollywood Beach Broadwalk that stretches nearly two and a half miles along the Atlantic. Named one of America’s Best Beach Boardwalk’s by Travel + Leisure magazine, this brick-paved thoroughfare is a haven for joggers, bicyclists, roller-bladers and all who’d prefer to take in the action from the comfort of one of the countless eateries and café’s along the way.

The easy ocean access and village-like feel make this a can’t miss destination with numerous highly-rated restaurants, small inns and hotels right on the broadwalk adding to its yesteryear charm. Family dining becomes stress-free, as Mom’s and Dad’s kick back to enjoy a seaside meal while their little ones entertain themselves in the sand just steps away. Two broadwalk parks attract kids of all ages to play paddleball at the historic Garfield Street courts or cool off in the whimsical dolphin play fountain. Locals rave about Josh’s Organic Market which sets up shop on the south end of the Hollywood Broadwalk every weekend selling garden fresh produce and blending a variety of mouth-watering exotic, tropical smoothies from its seaside stand. City leaders recently voted to move forward with a public/private partnership to build the first Jimmy Buffet Margaritaville Beach Resort on a six acre site on the broadwalk. This island-themed family-friendly resort will feature shops, restaurants and an immense outdoor entertainment area. A convenient Trolley service runs Wednesdays through Sundays, 10 a.m.-10 p.m. offering a nostalgic way to get to and from the best sites on the beach and downtown. For more information:

Call: (954) 924-2980 or visit www.visithollywoodfl.org

description:
Sanibel & Captiva are considered the shelling capital of North America. More than 300 species of shells can be found in the shallow water surrounding the islands.

The Bailey-Matthews Shell Museum is the only museum in the country dedicated entirely to shells. Over thirty exhibits tell the story of mollusks from around the world. Exhibits are devoted to shells in art and history, shell habitats, rare specimens, fossil shells and common Southwest Florida shells. Two live mollusk videos alternate continuously every 30 minutes.

Children are mesmerized by the children’s learning lab featuring a hands-on play area and a “live tank” with indigenous mollusks. This area provides a golden opportunity for children to experience the museum rather than merely observing exhibits. A half-hour video, Mollusks in Action, is shown on the hour and a children's video is shown continuously.

The museum is passionate about children’s education. The goal is for the museum to come alive as an exciting learning center instead of just a building.

Young girls are in awe when they discover that at one time shells were used as money and a bride’s value was calculated “in shells.” Many children stare in disbelief when learning that shells are actually made by a creature and the creature has a self propelling foot, a mouth and in the case of scallops, even eyes.

Summer Camps, Mommy and Me Play Sessions, a Youth Docent Program, half-day workshops, and a puppet theater are designed to help children discover the wonder of the world of shells. Children can even “shell-a-brate” their birthdays at the museum.

An exquisite gift shop offers a wide variety of unique shell-themed gifts including books, ceramics, clothing, toys and fine jewelry.

Open daily from 10 a.m. - 5 p.m. Thanksgiving, Christmas, New Year’s, Easter and the first Sunday in March are the only days the museum is closed. Admission is $7.00 for adults seventeen and up, $4.00 for youth five - 16 years of age and children four and under are free. Located close to “Ding” Darling National Wildlife Refuge. Call for program information or to register for classes. Visit their website for more information and a complete listing of programs and events.

Come experience Florida's Best Aquarium and one of the "top 5 kid-friendly aquariums in the country"! Encounter more than 20,000 aquatic plants and animals, from sharks to playful river otters. Enjoy daily penguin promenades, behind-the-scenes tours, dive shows, close-up animal encounters and two touch-tanks for hands-on experiences.
Certified SCUBA divers can Dive with the Sharks and those a little less adventurous can Swim with the Fishes in our largest exhibit, the 500,000-gallon Coral Reef. Come nose-to-nose with a green sea turtle while checking out the other 2,300 fish in crystal clear waters.

title: History of Fort Mose
address: 15 Fort Mose Trl., off of U.S. 1 North
description: The first free African settlement in North America and a premier site on the Florida Black Heritage trail. In 1738, the Spanish governor of Florida chartered Fort Mose as a settlement for freed Africans who had fled slavery in the British Carolinas. When Spain ceded Florida to Britain in 1763, the inhabitants of Fort Mose migrated to Cuba. Although nothing remains of the fort, the site was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1994 for its importance in American history.

title: Celery City Cruisers Car Show
description:
Sanford, one of Central Florida’s oldest incorporated cities, is home to brick-lined streets, towering oaks, elegant storefronts and many beautiful, nineteenth century Victorian homes. The picturesque downtown, which once featured feed stores and dry good sellers,now showcases unique shops, restaurants and art galleries. Events, such as the Saturday morning Farmers Market and jazz concerts in Magnolia Square; theatrical productions at the newly renovated Wayne Densch Performing Arts Center; the annual Greater Sanford Regional Chamber of Commerce Bikefest; and the monthly Alive After 5 street parties attract visitors from all over.
Sanford sits on the South shore of Lake Monroe, which provides a waterfront backdrop
for walking, jogging or just enjoying the natural beauty. RiverWalk, with its gazebos and swinging benches, has 1.2 miles of pedestrian walking paths. Along the way, you can visit Veterans Memorial Park, Marina Island, the Sanford Museum and Ft. Mellon Park with its new kid park and Splash Pad. Stop for lunch at one of the lakeside or nearby downtown restaurants.

With 38 diverse cities and towns, 47 miles of pristine beaches, and a staggering collection of attractions and cultural venues, the possibilities are endless. As America’s First Resort Destination® – established in 1894 – the area has spent decades perfecting the art of welcoming guests, and showing them the best way to experience Florida.

Known for legendary hospitality, the luxury and upscale hotels have enticed visitors to return year after year with their assurance of an unforgettable experience and world-class comfort. The sophistication and style of the enchanting boutique hotels is sure to impress you with choices from lavish to affordable or hip to historic.

Fine hotel brands are represented and deliver their trusted standards, amenities, service and value. Ideal for an intimate vacation or getaway, our small inns, B&Bs and vacation rentals offer the appeal of a home-away-from-home. title: Jazzed in Sanford
description:
Sanford, one of Central Florida’s oldest incorporated cities, is home to brick-lined streets, towering oaks, elegant storefronts and many beautiful, nineteenth century Victorian homes. The picturesque downtown, which once featured feed stores and dry good sellers,now showcases unique shops, restaurants and art galleries. Events, such as the Saturday morning Farmers Market and jazz concerts in Magnolia Square; theatrical productions at the newly renovated Wayne Densch Performing Arts Center; the annual Greater Sanford Regional Chamber of Commerce Bikefest; and the monthly Alive After 5 street parties attract visitors from all over.
Sanford sits on the South shore of Lake Monroe, which provides a waterfront backdrop
for walking, jogging or just enjoying the natural beauty. RiverWalk, with its gazebos and swinging benches, has 1.2 miles of pedestrian walking paths. Along the way, you can visit Veterans Memorial Park, Marina Island, the Sanford Museum and Ft. Mellon Park with its new kid park and Splash Pad. Stop for lunch at one of the lakeside or nearby downtown restaurants.

title: Ghost Story Tours
description:
DEERING ESTATE AT CUTLER
Located along the edge of Biscayne Bay, the 444-acre Deering Estate at Cutler is an environmental, archeological and historical preserve. From canoe rides to butterfly hikes, and nature guided tours, the Deering Estate has diverse activities for the whole family to enjoy. The Estate offers daily tours of the historic houses – the Stone House and Richmond Cottage, as well as naturalist lead tours of the lush natural areas where fossil bones have been found as far back at 50,000 years. The Estate is part of the Miami-Dade County Park and Recreation Department, which manages the Estate on behalf of the State of Florida. 

The Deering Estate is also a cultural and educational facility that features classes and programs for children and adults, teacher training and research opportunities. The Estate also serves as a small conference center for community organizations and corporate groups who share Charles Deering’s interest in the environment, botany, history, fine arts, antiques, rare books and wine. Rental of the Estate is available for special social functions. General admission includes tours of the historic homes and natural areas. Special eco-tours and guided canoe trips to the offshore island of Chicken Key are available for an additional fee. 16701 SW 72 Ave, Miami, FL 33157, 305-235-1668. www.deeringestate.org.

title: SudsFest
description:
Come experience Florida's Best Aquarium and one of the "top 5 kid-friendly aquariums in the country"! Whether exploring "the great outdoors" while inside our cool, air-conditioned facility or having a virtual encounter with a dolphin in our newest gallery, Ocean Commotion, The Florida Aquarium is a fabulous detination in the Tampa Bay area.
Encounter more than 20,000 aquatic plants and animals, from sharks to playful river otters. Enjoy daily penguin promenades, behind-the-scenes tours, dive shows, close-up animal encounters and two touch-tanks for hands-on experiences.
Certified SCUBA divers can Dive with the Sharks and those a little less adventurous can Swim with the Fishes in our largest exhibit, the 500,000-gallon Coral Reef. Come nose-to-nose with a green sea turtle while checking out the other 2,300 fish in crystal clear waters.
After looking at all that water inside, go outside and splash the day away in the 2-acre outdoor children's play area, Explore a Shore. Children can enjoy Florida sunshine while climbing aboard a 24-foot pirate ship, firing water canons or just playing in the water spouts with parents watching from the cool comfort of the full-service Cantina Bar and Grill.

title: Earth Day
description: Settled in 1894, this religious settlement boasted 50 buildings at one time, 11 of which still remain, including the Bakery, Art Hall and the restored home of founder Cyrus Reed Teed. title: Leif Erikson Festival
description: A unique riverfront community that is known for its genuine small-town charm and warm hospitality. The Jensen Beach, Hutchinson Island area is a top vacation destination with a perfect year-round climate, uncrowded natural beaches, great fishing, beautiful parks and a unique casual lifestyle. Commonly referred to as the "Art & Soul of Florida's Treasure Coast," Jensen Beach is a premier dining and one-of-a-kind retail destination, which includes art galleries, boutiques and a regional shopping mall. Jensen Beach is also well-known for hosting first-class events. The weekly street party, Jammin Jensen, is held down town every Thurs. evening. The Jensen Beach Pineapple Festival is the community's signature annual event held in Nov. The juried Jensen Beach Art & Craft Show is held in Jan. and the Taste of Jensen is held each Dec. The Jensen Beach Chamber of Commerce, located in historic downtown Jensen Beach, offers visitor and relocation information services.

title: Cabaret Concert Series
description:
DEERING ESTATE AT CUTLER
Located along the edge of Biscayne Bay, the 444-acre Deering Estate at Cutler is an environmental, archeological and historical preserve. From canoe rides to butterfly hikes, and nature guided tours, the Deering Estate has diverse activities for the whole family to enjoy. The Estate offers daily tours of the historic houses – the Stone House and Richmond Cottage, as well as naturalist lead tours of the lush natural areas where fossil bones have been found as far back at 50,000 years. The Estate is part of the Miami-Dade County Park and Recreation Department, which manages the Estate on behalf of the State of Florida. 

The Deering Estate is also a cultural and educational facility that features classes and programs for children and adults, teacher training and research opportunities. The Estate also serves as a small conference center for community organizations and corporate groups who share Charles Deering’s interest in the environment, botany, history, fine arts, antiques, rare books and wine. Rental of the Estate is available for special social functions. General admission includes tours of the historic homes and natural areas. title: Calling all Hunters
description:
OUR BEACH IS OIL FREE here in the middle of North Florida.  We have a white sandy beach with lots of blue water to enjoy.  Just the place for small children and older kids as well.  
   No sharks, no undertows, no waves, no salt water, just fresh water.  We keep our lake filled with a deep well.  With the ride down our 60 foot high water slide named The Tornado Slide you twist and turn down into the lake.  Great fun for everyone!!  This is a unique recreational campground resort, open year 'round, that offers beautiful surroundings, outdoor adventure and fun for the whole family. More than 175 RV camping sites situated among large oak trees with some lakeside sites. Offering 20/30/50 amp service. Rustic and deluxe cabins that sleep up to 16 guests. Grills at each site. title: Guided Hammock Walk
description: This 20-acre nature preserve, located on a barrier island on Boca Raton’s Intracoastal Waterway, is an experience you won’t want to miss. Sea turtles, sharks, stingray and other sea animals swim in their tanks. Take a stroll through the informal butterfly garden, walk along the boardwalk, climb the 40-foot observation tower and look out over the Atlantic Ocean and Intracoastal. The giant sea turtle garden is a wonderful place to learn about these fabulous endangered animals. They offer a variety of nature programs (reservations required) that appeal to all ages such as the popular nighttime Turtle Walk Program where you may see a turtle lay her eggs on the beach and the evening Hatchling Release Program, where they release baby sea turtles into the ocean. Check their website or call for class, workshop and trip information.  Injured and sick sea turtle are cared for in the Sea Turtle Rehabilitation Facility.

description:
DEERING ESTATE AT CUTLER
Located along the edge of Biscayne Bay, the 444-acre Deering Estate at Cutler is an environmental, archeological and historical preserve. From canoe rides to butterfly hikes, and nature guided tours, the Deering Estate has diverse activities for the whole family to enjoy. The Estate offers daily tours of the historic houses – the Stone House and Richmond Cottage, as well as naturalist lead tours of the lush natural areas where fossil bones have been found as far back at 50,000 years. The Estate is part of the Miami-Dade County Park and Recreation Department, which manages the Estate on behalf of the State of Florida. 

The Deering Estate is also a cultural and educational facility that features classes and programs for children and adults, teacher training and research opportunities. The Estate also serves as a small conference center for community organizations and corporate groups who share Charles Deering’s interest in the environment, botany, history, fine arts, antiques, rare books and wine. Rental of the Estate is available for special social functions. General admission includes tours of the historic homes and natural areas. Special eco-tours and guided canoe trips to the offshore island of Chicken Key are available for an additional fee. 16701 SW 72 Ave, Miami, FL 33157, 305-235-1668. www.deeringestate.org.

FRUIT & SPICE PARK
The only tropical botanical garden of its kind in the United States. The park exhibits 500 varieties of fruits, vegetables, spices, herbs, nuts, and other plant specimens from around the world. 24801 SW 187 Ave, Homestead, FL 33031, 305-247-5727. http://fruitandspicepark.org/friends/index.php

MIAMI-DADE PARKS ECOADVENTURES
EcoAdventures, anchored in Miami and established by the nationally renowned Miami-Dade Parks system, is one of the largest networks of parks, beaches, wildlife-landscapes, wetlands, and recreational gems in the entire United States. Masters of outdoor discovery, we are adventurers, educators and stewards of the fascinating subtropical South Florida ecosystem that is our wilderness playground. Nature is calling… Get EcoActive. 4000 Crandon Blvd. Key Biscayne, FL 33149. 305-365-3018. www.miamiecoadventures.com.

title: How, When & Where To Find Shells Workshop
description:
Sanibel & Captiva are considered the shelling capital of North America. More than 300 species of shells can be found in the shallow water surrounding the islands.

The Bailey-Matthews Shell Museum is the only museum in the country dedicated entirely to shells. Over thirty exhibits tell the story of mollusks from around the world. Exhibits are devoted to shells in art and history, shell habitats, rare specimens, fossil shells and common Southwest Florida shells. Two live mollusk videos alternate continuously every 30 minutes.

Children are mesmerized by the children’s learning lab featuring a hands-on play area and a “live tank” with indigenous mollusks. This area provides a golden opportunity for children to experience the museum rather than merely observing exhibits. A half-hour video, Mollusks in Action, is shown on the hour and a children's video is shown continuously.

The museum is passionate about children’s education. The goal is for the museum to come alive as an exciting learning center instead of just a building.

Young girls are in awe when they discover that at one time shells were used as money and a bride’s value was calculated “in shells.” Many children stare in disbelief when learning that shells are actually made by a creature and the creature has a self propelling foot, a mouth and in the case of scallops, even eyes.

Summer Camps, Mommy and Me Play Sessions, a Youth Docent Program, half-day workshops, and a puppet theater are designed to help children discover the wonder of the world of shells. Children can even “shell-a-brate” their birthdays at the museum.

An exquisite gift shop offers a wide variety of unique shell-themed gifts including books, ceramics, clothing, toys and fine jewelry.

Open daily from 10 a.m. - 5 p.m. Thanksgiving, Christmas, New Year’s, Easter and the first Sunday in March are the only days the museum is closed. Admission is $7.00 for adults seventeen and up, $4.00 for youth five - 16 years of age and children four and under are free. Located close to “Ding” Darling National Wildlife Refuge. Call for program information or to register for classes. Visit their website for more information and a complete listing of programs and events.

title: Celebrating the Arts: Fourth Fridays!
venue: Seminole County Convention and Visitors Bureau
description:
In the heart of Central Florida, Seminole County is quickly becoming a favorite destination. Whether you're looking for a newer hotel, at a better rate, the enjoyment of the natural wonders of a true Florida vacation, fine dining, miles of crystal clear rivers and wilderness trails, superb golf courses or simply to relax your mind and soul in our charming historic villages - it's easy to see why Seminole County is Florida's Natural Choice.

Located between the theme parks of Central Florida and the beautiful Treasure Coast beaches, access to Seminole County is a breeze. Whether visitors fly into hassle-free Sanford-Orlando International Airport or Orlando International, or arrive by Amtrak or by vehicle on I-4, the excitement is only a short hop away.

Visitors find many of the same flagship hotels and amenities as in Orlando, but often for a significantly lower rate. In addition to the excellent hotels that our guests currently enjoy, Seminole County has recently opened new hotels including a Hyatt Place, Residence Inn and a Westin.

Seminole County boasts 2,000 freshwater lakes and clear running rivers that create an abundance of outdoor activities. From kayaking to fishing, boating and hiking, the Wekiva River, Wekiva Springs State Park and other areas have become popular attractions. Showing a wilder side, flat-bottom airboats propel riders on an exhilarating trip in search of alligators and wildlife. A great new attraction located at the Central Florida Zoo and Botanical Gardens is ZOOm Air Adventures - an aerial adventure course that allows visitors to explore the tree tops from an animal's perspective. The only course of its kind in the United States, ZOOm Air is completely environmentally friendly and goes well beyond the usual zip line courses. For the less adventurous, the 1940's style Rivership Romance hosts luncheon and moonlight dinner cruises on the tranquil St. Johns River. Alternatively, the area hosts several golf courses, great antique shopping and charming villages with restaurants and nightlife for every taste.

Surrounded by the beauty of natural Florida, Seminole County offers the classic Florida experience.

title: History of Fort Mose
address: 15 Fort Mose Trl., off of U.S. 1 North
description: The first free African settlement in North America and a premier site on the Florida Black Heritage trail. In 1738, the Spanish governor of Florida chartered Fort Mose as a settlement for freed Africans who had fled slavery in the British Carolinas. When Spain ceded Florida to Britain in 1763, the inhabitants of Fort Mose migrated to Cuba. Although nothing remains of the fort, the site was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1994 for its importance in American history.

title: Gator Nights Join In Tour
description:
One-of-a-kind airboat tour in the heart of the Florida Everglades. Come visit this family owned and operated classic South Florida attraction deep in the swamp. With a recent half-million dollar renovation, Sawgrass now offers two exclusive adventures, the daytime Private Tour and the nighttime Red Eye Tour! Feel the excitement and learn the history of Florida's most remarkable treasure, the Everglades. As one of the rare subtropical ecosystems, the Everglades holds spectacular mysteries.
     Renew your spirit as you glide across miles of river at speeds up to 40 mph and get up close and personal with native wildlife. This once in a lifetime adventure will create lasting memories as you discover the secrets of this untamed wilderness. Start your adventure with a 30 minute airboat tour of the Florida Everglades. Your tour will be guided by one of the experienced captains who have received extensive training.
     During the tour, you'll listen to tales of how the Seminole and panther once coexisted in this lush wilderness. Also, you'll catch a glimpse of endangered wildlife as you skim across the glassy water. Take a walk on the wild side back in time with an original dinosaur, the Florida Alligator. The reptile exhibit features dozens of species both native and exotic to Florida. Along with their friendly turtles and iguanas, you can learn about Cannibal, their 1,000-pound alligator. 
     Handlers are happy to demonstrate how these animals live and survive in the wild. Be sure to bring your camera, so you can capture the excitement of you cradling one of these majestic animals with the "Hold a Baby Alligator" experience. 
     Your adventure will include a visit to the Exotic Wildlife exhibit. Predators Unlimited is a separate organization that brings a variety of animals to the park each day to visit. They strive to educate and enlighten the public about endangered species like the Florida Panther. Playful critters abound and amaze as you can see many different animals that often include panthers, lepoards and wolves.
     While you are at Sawgrass please don't miss the "Swamp"yard Island! You and your family can interact and feed many of their animals at this exhibit.

The High Springs Main Street program is a 501 (c) 3 non-profit under the Community Development Corporation.  The Main Street approach advocates improvements in four areas to create a positive, distinctive image for downtown:

1) Organization
2) Promotion
3) Design
4) Economic Restructuring

The Main Street approach also advocates a return to community self-reliance and emphasizes the downtown's traditional assets: personal service, local ownership, unique architecture, and sense of community. 

The Main Street Program Vision is to provide vibrant, economically-sustainable High Springs downtown district that respects and preserves its historical, small-town assets.

The Main Street Mission is to provide education, support, guidance and vision for the preservation, improvement and economic restructuring of the historical High Springs downtown district.

Discover The Palm Beaches and Boca Raton, an exciting collection of colorful resorts, matchless culinary delights, trendy shops and boutiques of world-wide fame, and a nightlife that thrives year-round. title: Free Lecture Series
description:
The Florida Carriage Museum & Resort encompasses over 400 acres of beauty in Central Florida’s horse country. Visitors to the Museum re-live history as they experience one of the finest collections of carriages in the world. They can even take a carriage ride (by prior appointment) on the winding roads through tall oaks draped in Spanish Moss, around the Qin Dynasty Gardens and past the exotic Japanese Koi Pond. Horses abound: a rare Poitou donkey named “Nicolette” and her best friend, a Miniature Horse named “Gracie”, welcome visitors and look for a scratch on the head.

The Museum houses one of the largest, privately owned collections of carriages in the world. It is open to the public and there are more than 160 meticulously restored carriages, including the 1840’s Dress Chariot formerly owned by Emperor Franz Joseph of Austria.

The Resort features 24 well appointed residences and 10 barns that serve as an equine “Bed & Barn.” Some guests bring their horses to train for the winter months, a weekend, or just for the day. Others come without horses to enjoy the miles of walking/carriage trails and can often be spotted picnicing under the shady oak trees.

description:
DEERING ESTATE AT CUTLER
Located along the edge of Biscayne Bay, the 444-acre Deering Estate at Cutler is an environmental, archeological and historical preserve. From canoe rides to butterfly hikes, and nature guided tours, the Deering Estate has diverse activities for the whole family to enjoy. The Estate offers daily tours of the historic houses – the Stone House and Richmond Cottage, as well as naturalist lead tours of the lush natural areas where fossil bones have been found as far back at 50,000 years. The Estate is part of the Miami-Dade County Park and Recreation Department, which manages the Estate on behalf of the State of Florida. 

The Deering Estate is also a cultural and educational facility that features classes and programs for children and adults, teacher training and research opportunities. The Estate also serves as a small conference center for community organizations and corporate groups who share Charles Deering’s interest in the environment, botany, history, fine arts, antiques, rare books and wine. Rental of the Estate is available for special social functions. General admission includes tours of the historic homes and natural areas. Special eco-tours and guided canoe trips to the offshore island of Chicken Key are available for an additional fee. 16701 SW 72 Ave, Miami, FL 33157, 305-235-1668. www.deeringestate.org.

FRUIT & SPICE PARK
The only tropical botanical garden of its kind in the United States. The park exhibits 500 varieties of fruits, vegetables, spices, herbs, nuts, and other plant specimens from around the world. 24801 SW 187 Ave, Homestead, FL 33031, 305-247-5727. http://fruitandspicepark.org/friends/index.php

MIAMI-DADE PARKS ECOADVENTURES
EcoAdventures, anchored in Miami and established by the nationally renowned Miami-Dade Parks system, is one of the largest networks of parks, beaches, wildlife-landscapes, wetlands, and recreational gems in the entire United States. Masters of outdoor discovery, we are adventurers, educators and stewards of the fascinating subtropical South Florida ecosystem that is our wilderness playground. Nature is calling… Get EcoActive. 4000 Crandon Blvd. Key Biscayne, FL 33149. 305-365-3018. www.miamiecoadventures.com.

description:
Hollywood is a classic Florida beachtown that’s enchanted visitors since the 1920s. Visitors love the Hollywood Trolley which provides a scenic way to enjoy the best of Hollywood Beach and Downtown. Hollywood Beach features a one-of-a-kind oceanfront promenade called the Hollywood Beach Broadwalk that stretches nearly two and a half miles along the Atlantic. Named one of America’s Best Beach Boardwalk’s by Travel + Leisure magazine, this brick-paved thoroughfare is a haven for joggers, bicyclists, roller-bladers and all who’d prefer to take in the action from the comfort of one of the countless eateries and café’s along the way.

The easy ocean access and village-like feel make this a can’t miss destination with numerous highly-rated restaurants, small inns and hotels right on the broadwalk adding to its yesteryear charm. Family dining becomes stress-free, as Mom’s and Dad’s kick back to enjoy a seaside meal while their little ones entertain themselves in the sand just steps away. Two broadwalk parks attract kids of all ages to play paddleball at the historic Garfield Street courts or cool off in the whimsical dolphin play fountain. Locals rave about Josh’s Organic Market which sets up shop on the south end of the Hollywood Broadwalk every weekend selling garden fresh produce and blending a variety of mouth-watering exotic, tropical smoothies from its seaside stand. City leaders recently voted to move forward with a public/private partnership to build the first Jimmy Buffet Margaritaville Beach Resort on a six acre site on the broadwalk. This island-themed family-friendly resort will feature shops, restaurants and an immense outdoor entertainment area. A convenient Trolley service runs Wednesdays through Sundays, 10 a.m.-10 p.m. offering a nostalgic way to get to and from the best sites on the beach and downtown. For more information:

Call: (954) 924-2980 or visit www.visithollywoodfl.org

Florida's premiere aviation attraction showcases vintage aircraft from the world’s largest private collection. General admission includes flight simulators, interactive exhibits, a tram tour of aircraft maintenance areas, restoration and backlot tours and a daily aerial demonstration - a unique opportunity to see rare aircraft in flight (weather permitting). Sight and sound immersion experiences bring you back in time to Early Flight, the trenches of WWI and even on board a B-17 in a WWII bombing mission.
 
Recent additions to Fantasy of Flight attractions include audio tours, the Fun with Flight center for families, The Tuskegee Airmen – They Dared to Fly exhibit and the multimedia tribute to the WASP (Women Airforce Service Pilots) – A Passionate Pursuit.
 
Visit the Art Deco-styled Compass Rose Diner from 11 a.m.-3 p.m. daily, or Fantasy of Flight’s Gift Shop for specialty product offerings for your favorite aviation enthusiast. Both are open to the public, with no admission fee required. Parking is free (excluding special events). Hot air balloon rides and biplane rides are available for an extra charge.

Sanford, one of Central Florida’s oldest incorporated cities, is home to brick-lined streets, towering oaks, elegant storefronts and many beautiful, nineteenth century Victorian homes. The picturesque downtown, which once featured feed stores and dry good sellers,now showcases unique shops, restaurants and art galleries. Events, such as the Saturday morning Farmers Market and jazz concerts in Magnolia Square; theatrical productions at the newly renovated Wayne Densch Performing Arts Center; the annual Greater Sanford Regional Chamber of Commerce Bikefest; and the monthly Alive After 5 street parties attract visitors from all over.
Sanford sits on the South shore of Lake Monroe, which provides a waterfront backdrop
for walking, jogging or just enjoying the natural beauty. RiverWalk, with its gazebos and swinging benches, has 1.2 miles of pedestrian walking paths. Along the way, you can visit Veterans Memorial Park, Marina Island, the Sanford Museum and Ft. Mellon Park with its new kid park and Splash Pad. Stop for lunch at one of the lakeside or nearby downtown restaurants.

title: Women\'s Half Marathon and 5K
description:
Mako's Vista Beach Condo/Resort Rentals specializes in privately owned rentals located within  Sunset Vista Beachfront Resort where each unit is individually owned and operated. 

We welcome you to bask in the warm Florida sun at our spectacular beachfront resort on Treasure Island, right in the heart of the Clearwater/St. Petersburg beach resort area. Famous for the white powder sands and stunning sunsets, this is the perfect destination for your sun coast vacation!

Every “Tommy Bahama”-style suite provides two bedrooms and two bathrooms, a separate living/dining room with a queen sofa bed, a fully furnished kitchen complete with granite countertops, washer/dryer and a private balcony with a breathtaking view of the Gulf of Mexico.

At Sunset Vistas you can cool off in a large resort swimming pool, a one of a kind childrens wading pool with fountains, relax in one of two of our whirlpool spas, revitalize in the spacious fitness center or refresh yourself by the fountains in the tropical courtyard. Satisfy your cravings at our café and sample a tropical cocktail at the beach bar.

The majority of our units feature free local and long distance calling in the USA and Canada and free wired internet.  Please inquire at the time of booking if you require this feature.  We also offer complimentary internet access available in the cafe and business center. 

Explore some of the world’s finest beaches, parasail or jet ski, fish from nearby John’s Pass Fishing and Shopping Village or experience the unique Salvador Dali and Florida International Museums.

Busch Gardens and an array of attractions are easily accessible. Golf, Tennis and Tropicana Field (home of the Tampa Bay Devil Rays) and Raymond James Stadium (home of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers) are only minutes away!

title: Florida\'s Creative Coast Getaway Weekend
venue: Greater Pine Island Chamber of Commerce
description: Located just 30 minutes from Fort Myers, but the secluded, small-town atmosphere is a world apart. Surrounded by mangroves, three aquatic preserves and with mostly agricultural zoning, it has escaped the development of other Florida islands. Pine Island consists of five communities: Matlacha, Center, Bokeelia, Pineland, St. James City. Each is unique and special, yet all are Pine Island. Pine Island boasts "no high-rises and no traffic lights." Art, music and kayaking are all popular.

title: Monthly Wine Dinner
description:
Azure restaurant and lounge offer upscale dining in a relaxed oceanfront indoor and al fresco atmosphere. A favorite of locals, the menu offers sustainable options of chef-inspired daily inspirations and popular meat and fresh seafood dishes.

The restaurant is also open for breakfast and lunch and the poolside Tiki Hut is a casual spot for your favorite frozen beverage, salads and grilled sanwiches.

"S'mores at The Shores" is a signature pasttime at the beachfrom firepits - especially popular for families.

title: Big Cypress Shootout
address: Big Cypress Seminole Indian Reservation, between Fort Lauderdale and Naples off of I-75 (at Exit 49) then north 19 miles
description: A 2,200 acre eco-heritage wildlife park located in the Florida Everglades on the Big Cypress Seminole Indian Reservation, Billie Swamp Safari offers swamp buggy eco-tours and airboat rides through untamed Everglades plus snake & alligator shows, swamp critter shows, nature trail, animal and reptile exhibits, day packages and overnight stays in authentic thatched roof chickees.  Exclusive tours are available.  Dine in the Swamp Water Cafe and stop by the gift shop for Everglades souvenirs before leaving.  800-GO-SAFARI, www.billieswampsafari.travel.  Located off of I-75 between Naples and Fort Lauderdale.

title: WILL McLEAN MUSIC FESTIVAL
description: Take it easy 'naturally'! Bordered by the Gulf of Mexico and the Withlacoochee River, Hernando County offers a cornucopia for nature enthusiasts. Rolling hills, sawgrass salt marshes, crystal clear springs, whispering forests, parks and trails provide hiking, birding, water recreation, golf, camping, biking and breathtaking sunsets. Brooksville's hometown atmosphere renders oak-canopied streets, unique shopping, history, art, events and cozy dining. Be enchanted by the Weeki Wachee Mermaids and enjoy Florida's only natural spring water park. Visit Hernando County with access to all major Florida attractions.

title: Sea Turtle Day
description: This 20-acre nature preserve, located on a barrier island on Boca Raton’s Intracoastal Waterway, is an experience you won’t want to miss. Sea turtles, sharks, stingray and other sea animals swim in their tanks. Take a stroll through the informal butterfly garden, walk along the boardwalk, climb the 40-foot observation tower and look out over the Atlantic Ocean and Intracoastal. The giant sea turtle garden is a wonderful place to learn about these fabulous endangered animals. They offer a variety of nature programs (reservations required) that appeal to all ages such as the popular nighttime Turtle Walk Program where you may see a turtle lay her eggs on the beach and the evening Hatchling Release Program, where they release baby sea turtles into the ocean. Check their website or call for class, workshop and trip information.  Injured and sick sea turtle are cared for in the Sea Turtle Rehabilitation Facility.

title: HOMOSASSA HERITAGE DAY
venue: Ellie Schiller Homosassa Springs Wildlife State Park
description: Meet a manatee up close, face-to-face, underwater without even getting wet. This Florida State Park is a showcase for Florida's native wildlife in a natural setting of woods and wetlands. Stroll along the Wildlife Walk to view black bears, foxes, river otters, cougars, bobcats, key deer and hundreds of birds. New additions of endangered species include a Florida panther, three d Red wolves, and two Whooping cranes. Daily educational programs on manatees, alligators and Florida snakes. Pontoon boats from Visitor Center to wildlife park, weather permitting.

title: 15th Annual Young Artist Music Series
description: An extraordinary blend of art, architecture, history and ecology. This 35-acre subtropical estate and historic house museum was designed by Frederic Clay Bartlett, a noted painter and art collector. Bonnet House is one of the few complete homes and studios of two American artists with original furnishings open to the public. A nature trail walk taking up to 30 minutes is available. Guided golf cart tour of nature trail available. Outdoor rental space available.

title: Springs Celebration
description: Located on the banks of the scenic and unique Santa Fe River, a tributary of the Suwannee River. Within O'Leno, the Santa Fe disappears and flows underground for more than three miles before it again becomes a surface stream at the River Rise. Fishing is allowed along the banks of the river (except in the swimming area) and in any of the many sinkhole ponds throughout the park. You may also launch a canoe (when the river is high enough) and fish upstream from the picnic area. Fish commonly caught are bass, brim and catfish.

title: SunFest
venue: Palm Beach County Convention & Visitors Bureau
description:
Discover The Palm Beaches and Boca Raton, an exciting collection of colorful resorts, matchless culinary delights, trendy shops and boutiques of world-wide fame, and a nightlife that thrives year-round. With 38 diverse cities and towns, 47 miles of pristine beaches, and a staggering collection of attractions and cultural venues, the possibilities are endless. As America’s First Resort Destination® – established in 1894 – the area has spent decades perfecting the art of welcoming guests, and showing them the best way to experience Florida.

Known for legendary hospitality, the luxury and upscale hotels have enticed visitors to return year after year with their assurance of an unforgettable experience and world-class comfort. The sophistication and style of the enchanting boutique hotels is sure to impress you with choices from lavish to affordable or hip to historic.

Fine hotel brands are represented and deliver their trusted standards, amenities, service and value. Our distinctive hotels will tempt you to stay just a little bit longer with their charm and local ambiance. Ideal for an intimate vacation or getaway, our small inns, B&Bs and vacation rentals offer the appeal of a home-away-from-home. Whether looking for an activity-filled campground or a secluded, private location, there is something for everyone.

Discover your vacation experience. We are the gateway to the Florida Everglades. Ecotourism and natural attractions lure the adventurer in all of us; whether it be strolling through a natural preserve or catching bass in Lake Okeechobee. The Palm Beaches boasts more than 170 public and private golf courses— from executive to championship level— throughout its expansive, nearly 2,000 square miles of picturesque territory. With world-famous equestrian and tennis facilities, the destination provide a large scope of sporting activities. If your travel passions are cultural, culinary or sporting, there is a top-notched event of festival to suit you. Considered Florida’s Cultural Capital, the Palm Beaches and Boca Raton are also home to more than 200 theaters, museums, arts centers, indoor and outdoor performance stages and other cultural venues.

Come to The Palm Beaches and Boca Raton and come experience our hospitality and affordability. Discover the best of everything and the best way to experience Florida.

title: Natural Science Lecture Series:  \"The Effect of the Deepwater Horizon Spill on the Deep Coral Communities in the Gulf of Mexico.
description:
Sanibel & Captiva are considered the shelling capital of North America. More than 300 species of shells can be found in the shallow water surrounding the islands.

The Bailey-Matthews Shell Museum is the only museum in the country dedicated entirely to shells. Over thirty exhibits tell the story of mollusks from around the world. Exhibits are devoted to shells in art and history, shell habitats, rare specimens, fossil shells and common Southwest Florida shells. Two live mollusk videos alternate continuously every 30 minutes.

Children are mesmerized by the children’s learning lab featuring a hands-on play area and a “live tank” with indigenous mollusks. This area provides a golden opportunity for children to experience the museum rather than merely observing exhibits. A half-hour video, Mollusks in Action, is shown on the hour and a children's video is shown continuously.

The museum is passionate about children’s education. The goal is for the museum to come alive as an exciting learning center instead of just a building.

Young girls are in awe when they discover that at one time shells were used as money and a bride’s value was calculated “in shells.” Many children stare in disbelief when learning that shells are actually made by a creature and the creature has a self propelling foot, a mouth and in the case of scallops, even eyes.

Summer Camps, Mommy and Me Play Sessions, a Youth Docent Program, half-day workshops, and a puppet theater are designed to help children discover the wonder of the world of shells. Children can even “shell-a-brate” their birthdays at the museum.

An exquisite gift shop offers a wide variety of unique shell-themed gifts including books, ceramics, clothing, toys and fine jewelry.

Open daily from 10 a.m. - 5 p.m. Thanksgiving, Christmas, New Year’s, Easter and the first Sunday in March are the only days the museum is closed. Admission is $7.00 for adults seventeen and up, $4.00 for youth five - 16 years of age and children four and under are free. Located close to “Ding” Darling National Wildlife Refuge. Call for program information or to register for classes. Visit their website for more information and a complete listing of programs and events.
