At the northern end of the Tampa Bay area, beautiful Pasco County is close to major cities but far from the hustle and bustle. Visit Pasco and enjoy Florida the way it used to be. Acres of pristine wilderness with biking, hiking and canoeing trails. Historic downtowns with fine restaurants and antique shops and dozens of family-oriented activities and sporting events year 'round. Pasco County is home to world-class tennis and golf resorts, including Saddlebrook Resort & Spa, one of Conde Nast Traveler's Top 100 and Lake Jovita, the Florida course that plays like North Carolina. 


Enjoy cultural treasures, such as the Historic Courthouse, built in 1909 in beautiful downtown Dade City and the Pioneer Florida Museum, home to period buildings dating to 1878. Experience historic walking tours of downtown New Port Richey, boat tours of the Pithlachascotee River and trolley tours in downtown Dade City. See the World War II Barracks Museum in Zephyrhills, the St. Leo Abbey & Grotto in St. Leo and an original "Cracker House'' in Holiday. Camp at Starkey Wilderness Park, cast your fishing line at Anclote River Park, paddle a kayak at Werner Boyce Salt Spring State Park. Hike the Suncoast Trail, visit spots along the Great Florida Birding Trail or charter a deep sea fishing excursion.


From the beaches on the Gulf Coast to scenic rivers like the Withlacoochee in the east to one of the world's premier drop zones at Skydive City, Pasco has something for everyone. See local and national acts perform at the Show Palace in Hudson and historic Richey Suncoast Theater in New Port Richey. Savor locally-made wines at the Florida Estates Winery in Land O' Lakes. Enjoy dozens of unique festivals, including Chasco Fiesta in New Port Richey and the Kumquat Festival in Dade City.

title: Safety Harbor Seafood Festival
description:
Safety Harbor is located by the sheltered inlets of Old Tampa Bay, on the “sunrise side of the bay” as the locals say.  Its colorful history includes Native American tribe headquarters, Spanish explorers, pirates, healing waters and the first grapefruit ever planted in Florida.


The community itself is welcoming and picturesque.  A beautiful waterfront park and marina offer excellent views of the bay as well as being a popular spot for viewing manatee in the summer months.  Next to the marina is the historic Safety Harbor Resort and Spa, a historical property situated on the site of ancient mineral springs once discovered by Spanish explorers in their quest for "the fountain of youth".  The mineral waters are still used today for spa treatments and drinking water.


Downtown Safety Harbor is definitely for walking.  Art galleries, shops, boutiques, a much-used pavilion and one of the largest live oak trees in existence can be found within several blocks.  The Chamber and welcome center provide brochures, visitor information and area gifts for purchase.  Restaurants and cafes abound; many are locally owned and offer outside dining.


The Safety Harbor Regional Museum of History offers a glimpse into the early development of the area and showcases artifacts, dioramas, and artwork dating to the 1500s.  The museum sits on the site of a Tocoboga Indian mound.


The very popular Philippe Park, a 122-acre county-run park, flanks scenic Tampa Bay and features scenic picnic shelters, playground, boat ramp and walking trails.  A raised Indian mound is on the site, as is the gravesite of Odet Philippe, whose land grant and subsequent developed citrus grove resulted in the first grapefruit ever planted in Florida.  Philippe has been inducted into the Florida Citrus Hall of Fame for his contributions to what is now a billion-dollar citrus industry in Florida.


For a small town with population under 20,000, Safety Harbor hosts many events throughout the year including the annual wine festival, HarbourSounds music festival and other family events.  On the third Friday of each month, the Main Street is closed down to street traffic and is lined with arts and crafts booths, food vendors, and entertainment.  A seasonal farmer's market is held by the pavilion throughout the cooler months.  Only 20 minutes from TPA and PIE airports and 30 minutes from Clearwater Beach, Safety Harbor is a perfect getaway.

title: PrideFest
description:
There was a time, not so long ago, when hospitality and service were expected to be an effortless part of the hotel experience. Guests were greeted with warm smiles from the moment they walked through the doors. Cocktails were served in the wood paneled bar, guests took breakfast on the patio, and dinner was an elegant affair. The Riverside has continued to uphold these fine standards. Since opening its doors in 1936, its name became synonymous with charm and elegance. And in the 72 years since, absolutely nothing has changed. Today, the Riverside Hotel remains a beacon of old world civility in a thriving, modern and beautiful destination, combining the highest levels of service with elegant accommodations, exquisite cuisine and prime location on the river in the heart of Fort Lauderdale’s downtown.
The Riverside is the city’s oldest hotel, built on the well-known Las Olas Boulevard dining and shopping district. An island in a sea of ultra modern skyscrapers, Las Olas offers a taste of Old Florida. It’s a place where professionals conduct business, whether dealing in local service or international markets. And it’s a place where travelers from across the globe come to discover the richness of South Florida. Situated on the banks of the New River, the Riverside Hotel is only blocks from Fort Lauderdale’s central business district. Guests can stroll the mile-long Riverwalk which leads from the pioneer Stranahan House to the acclaimed Broward Center for the Performing Arts, the Museum of Discovery and Science and IMAX Theater, the Fort Lauderdale Museum of Art, and the Broward County Main Library. The hotel is just minutes from the Fort Lauderdale/Hollywood International Airport, Port Everglades International Cruise Port and the Broward County Convention Center.

DEERING ESTATE AT CUTLER
Located along the edge of Biscayne Bay, the 444-acre Deering Estate at Cutler is an environmental, archeological and historical preserve. From canoe rides to butterfly hikes, and nature guided tours, the Deering Estate has diverse activities for the whole family to enjoy. The Estate offers daily tours of the historic houses – the Stone House and Richmond Cottage, as well as naturalist lead tours of the lush natural areas where fossil bones have been found as far back at 50,000 years. The Estate is part of the Miami-Dade County Park and Recreation Department, which manages the Estate on behalf of the State of Florida. 

The Deering Estate is also a cultural and educational facility that features classes and programs for children and adults, teacher training and research opportunities. The Estate also serves as a small conference center for community organizations and corporate groups who share Charles Deering’s interest in the environment, botany, history, fine arts, antiques, rare books and wine. Rental of the Estate is available for special social functions. General admission includes tours of the historic homes and natural areas. Special eco-tours and guided canoe trips to the offshore island of Chicken Key are available for an additional fee. 16701 SW 72 Ave, Miami, FL 33157, 305-235-1668. www.deeringestate.org.

The only tropical botanical garden of its kind in the United States. The park exhibits 500 varieties of fruits, vegetables, spices, herbs, nuts, and other plant specimens from around the world. 24801 SW 187 Ave, Homestead, FL 33031, 305-247-5727. http://fruitandspicepark.org/friends/index.php

description:
Safety Harbor is located by the sheltered inlets of Old Tampa Bay, on the “sunrise side of the bay” as the locals say.  Its colorful history includes Native American tribe headquarters, Spanish explorers, pirates, healing waters and the first grapefruit ever planted in Florida.


The community itself is welcoming and picturesque.  A beautiful waterfront park and marina offer excellent views of the bay as well as being a popular spot for viewing manatee in the summer months.  Next to the marina is the historic Safety Harbor Resort and Spa, a historical property situated on the site of ancient mineral springs once discovered by Spanish explorers in their quest for "the fountain of youth".  The mineral waters are still used today for spa treatments and drinking water.


Downtown Safety Harbor is definitely for walking.  Art galleries, shops, boutiques, a much-used pavilion and one of the largest live oak trees in existence can be found within several blocks.  The Chamber and welcome center provide brochures, visitor information and area gifts for purchase.  Restaurants and cafes abound; many are locally owned and offer outside dining.


The Safety Harbor Regional Museum of History offers a glimpse into the early development of the area and showcases artifacts, dioramas, and artwork dating to the 1500s.  The museum sits on the site of a Tocoboga Indian mound.


The very popular Philippe Park, a 122-acre county-run park, flanks scenic Tampa Bay and features scenic picnic shelters, playground, boat ramp and walking trails.  A raised Indian mound is on the site, as is the gravesite of Odet Philippe, whose land grant and subsequent developed citrus grove resulted in the first grapefruit ever planted in Florida.  Philippe has been inducted into the Florida Citrus Hall of Fame for his contributions to what is now a billion-dollar citrus industry in Florida.


For a small town with population under 20,000, Safety Harbor hosts many events throughout the year including the annual wine festival, HarbourSounds music festival and other family events.  On the third Friday of each month, the Main Street is closed down to street traffic and is lined with arts and crafts booths, food vendors, and entertainment.  A seasonal farmer's market is held by the pavilion throughout the cooler months.  Only 20 minutes from TPA and PIE airports and 30 minutes from Clearwater Beach, Safety Harbor is a perfect getaway.

description: The museum and the park's 1863 cracker homestead interpret the areas' natural and cultural history. The museum interprets the history of forestry in North Florida and offers a fundamental understanding of the evolution and ecology of the forest. The museum showcases early turpentine production with a model still and antique tools of the trade. Many of the products that are produced from the long leaf pine tree are displayed along with rare old photographs of early logging operations. The exhibits are educational and entertaining. Young and old will enjoy the still wildlife exhibits and Terrie the talking tree, with her message about the importance of trees in our environment. The octagonal shaped museum with its high-glass dome ceiling showcases a variety of Florida wood in both its exhibits and the museum's construction. The 1863 cracker homestead with its antique tools and furnishings will take you back in time to the days of Florida's early settlers. The park is beautifully landscaped with long leaf pines, beds of cootie ferns, a manicured lawn and a variety of native plants and trees. title: Story of Jesus
Wicked
description:
There was a time, not so long ago, when hospitality and service were expected to be an effortless part of the hotel experience. Guests were greeted with warm smiles from the moment they walked through the doors. Cocktails were served in the wood paneled bar, guests took breakfast on the patio, and dinner was an elegant affair. The Riverside has continued to uphold these fine standards. Since opening its doors in 1936, its name became synonymous with charm and elegance. And in the 72 years since, absolutely nothing has changed. Today, the Riverside Hotel remains a beacon of old world civility in a thriving, modern and beautiful destination, combining the highest levels of service with elegant accommodations, exquisite cuisine and prime location on the river in the heart of Fort Lauderdale’s downtown.
The Riverside is the city’s oldest hotel, built on the well-known Las Olas Boulevard dining and shopping district. An island in a sea of ultra modern skyscrapers, Las Olas offers a taste of Old Florida. It’s a place where professionals conduct business, whether dealing in local service or international markets. And it’s a place where travelers from across the globe come to discover the richness of South Florida. Situated on the banks of the New River, the Riverside Hotel is only blocks from Fort Lauderdale’s central business district. Guests can stroll the mile-long Riverwalk which leads from the pioneer Stranahan House to the acclaimed Broward Center for the Performing Arts, the Museum of Discovery and Science and IMAX Theater, the Fort Lauderdale Museum of Art, and the Broward County Main Library. The hotel is just minutes from the Fort Lauderdale/Hollywood International Airport, Port Everglades International Cruise Port and the Broward County Convention Center.
The Riverside Hotel can always be counted on for the quality, service and ambience of its unique and popular restaurants. Indigo restaurant serves traditional breakfast, lunch and dinner. The Grill Room on Las Olas is a Four Diamond AAA award recipient-for the ninth consecutive year, serves only the best quality seafood and meats complemented by an extensive wine list. The Golden Lyon Bar is a cozy gathering place where guests can enjoy cocktails and appetizers. Preston’s Lounge is located in the lobby where you can also enjoy cocktails, appetizers and great conversation.

description:
At the northern end of the Tampa Bay area, beautiful Pasco County is close to major cities but far from the hustle and bustle. Visit Pasco and enjoy Florida the way it used to be. Acres of pristine wilderness with biking, hiking and canoeing trails. Historic downtowns with fine restaurants and antique shops and dozens of family-oriented activities and sporting events year 'round. Pasco County is home to world-class tennis and golf resorts, including Saddlebrook Resort & Spa, one of Conde Nast Traveler's Top 100 and Lake Jovita, the Florida course that plays like North Carolina. 


Enjoy cultural treasures, such as the Historic Courthouse, built in 1909 in beautiful downtown Dade City and the Pioneer Florida Museum, home to period buildings dating to 1878. Camp at Starkey Wilderness Park, cast your fishing line at Anclote River Park, paddle a kayak at Werner Boyce Salt Spring State Park. Hike the Suncoast Trail, visit spots along the Great Florida Birding Trail or charter a deep sea fishing excursion.


From the beaches on the Gulf Coast to scenic rivers like the Withlacoochee in the east to one of the world's premier drop zones at Skydive City, Pasco has something for everyone. See local and national acts perform at the Show Palace in Hudson and historic Richey Suncoast Theater in New Port Richey. Savor locally-made wines at the Florida Estates Winery in Land O' Lakes. Enjoy dozens of unique festivals, including Chasco Fiesta in New Port Richey and the Kumquat Festival in Dade City.

description:
Florida's premiere aviation attraction showcases vintage aircraft from the world’s largest private collection. General admission includes flight simulators, interactive exhibits, a tram tour of aircraft maintenance areas, restoration and backlot tours and a daily aerial demonstration - a unique opportunity to see rare aircraft in flight (weather permitting). Sight and sound immersion experiences bring you back in time to Early Flight, the trenches of WWI and even on board a B-17 in a WWII bombing mission.
 
Recent additions to Fantasy of Flight attractions include audio tours, the Fun with Flight center for families, The Tuskegee Airmen – They Dared to Fly exhibit and the multimedia tribute to the WASP (Women Airforce Service Pilots) – A Passionate Pursuit.
 
Visit the Art Deco-styled Compass Rose Diner from 11 a.m.-3 p.m. daily, or Fantasy of Flight’s Gift Shop for specialty product offerings for your favorite aviation enthusiast. title: Archaeology Day
description:
DEERING ESTATE AT CUTLER
Located along the edge of Biscayne Bay, the 444-acre Deering Estate at Cutler is an environmental, archeological and historical preserve. From canoe rides to butterfly hikes, and nature guided tours, the Deering Estate has diverse activities for the whole family to enjoy. The Estate offers daily tours of the historic houses – the Stone House and Richmond Cottage, as well as naturalist lead tours of the lush natural areas where fossil bones have been found as far back at 50,000 years. The Estate is part of the Miami-Dade County Park and Recreation Department, which manages the Estate on behalf of the State of Florida. 

The Deering Estate is also a cultural and educational facility that features classes and programs for children and adults, teacher training and research opportunities. The Estate also serves as a small conference center for community organizations and corporate groups who share Charles Deering’s interest in the environment, botany, history, fine arts, antiques, rare books and wine. Rental of the Estate is available for special social functions. General admission includes tours of the historic homes and natural areas. Special eco-tours and guided canoe trips to the offshore island of Chicken Key are available for an additional fee. 16701 SW 72 Ave, Miami, FL 33157, 305-235-1668. www.deeringestate.org.

Masters of outdoor discovery, we are adventurers, educators and stewards of the fascinating subtropical South Florida ecosystem that is our wilderness playground. title: Kiwanis Arts & Crafts Show
description:
Safety Harbor is located by the sheltered inlets of Old Tampa Bay, on the “sunrise side of the bay” as the locals say.  Its colorful history includes Native American tribe headquarters, Spanish explorers, pirates, healing waters and the first grapefruit ever planted in Florida.


The community itself is welcoming and picturesque.  A beautiful waterfront park and marina offer excellent views of the bay as well as being a popular spot for viewing manatee in the summer months.  Next to the marina is the historic Safety Harbor Resort and Spa, a historical property situated on the site of ancient mineral springs once discovered by Spanish explorers in their quest for "the fountain of youth".  The mineral waters are still used today for spa treatments and drinking water.


Downtown Safety Harbor is definitely for walking.  Art galleries, shops, boutiques, a much-used pavilion and one of the largest live oak trees in existence can be found within several blocks.  The Chamber and welcome center provide brochures, visitor information and area gifts for purchase.  Restaurants and cafes abound; many are locally owned and offer outside dining.


The Safety Harbor Regional Museum of History offers a glimpse into the early development of the area and showcases artifacts, dioramas, and artwork dating to the 1500s.  The museum sits on the site of a Tocoboga Indian mound.


The very popular Philippe Park, a 122-acre county-run park, flanks scenic Tampa Bay and features scenic picnic shelters, playground, boat ramp and walking trails.  A raised Indian mound is on the site, as is the gravesite of Odet Philippe, whose land grant and subsequent developed citrus grove resulted in the first grapefruit ever planted in Florida.  Philippe has been inducted into the Florida Citrus Hall of Fame for his contributions to what is now a billion-dollar citrus industry in Florida.


For a small town with population under 20,000, Safety Harbor hosts many events throughout the year including the annual wine festival, HarbourSounds music festival and other family events.  On the third Friday of each month, the Main Street is closed down to street traffic and is lined with arts and crafts booths, food vendors, and entertainment.  A seasonal farmer's market is held by the pavilion throughout the cooler months.  Only 20 minutes from TPA and PIE airports and 30 minutes from Clearwater Beach, Safety Harbor is a perfect getaway.

title: Wild Animals Hunt for Easter Eggs at Naples Zoo
description:
Much more than a walk-thru zoo, this historic tropical garden with mature botanicals and nationally accredited zoo features a full day of wildlife experiences to delight guests with the natural world to inspire the conservation of our planet's remaining wild areas and their wondrous inhabitants. 


Daily presentations include the hand-feeding of giant reptiles at Alligator Bay, Meet the Keeper Series, Snake Sunbathing, along with two premiere presentations in the Safari Canyon theater where guests see live animals from feline predators to venomous snakes along with exciting video footage. A guided tour of the historic garden is offered on Sundays. One of the zoo’s most popular activities is the Primate Expedition Cruise where guests embark on a guided cruise past islands inhabited by monkeys, lemurs, and apes. Guests enjoy seeing favorites like lions, monkeys, zebras, and the new Giraffe Preview Exhibit. They also discover rarely seen species like Malagasy fosas and Parma wallabies. At large glass walls, they get wildly close to carnivores at exhibits like Leopard Rock, Tiger Forest, Black Bear Hammock, and Panther Glade.


Along with all that’s new, Naples Zoo has a wonderful history beginning in 1919 when botanist Dr. Henry Nehrling founded the garden. After his death, the trees grew wild until a Fleischmann Yeast heir expanded the forgotten garden in 1954. In 1969, Lawrence and Nancy Jane Tetzlaff, a.k.a. Jungle Larry and Safari Jane, introduced the wild animals. Larry did stunt work for Johnny Weissmuller in the famous Tarzan films, milked thousands of venomous snakes during WWII, and educated millions of adults and children throughout the Midwest and Florida with his wife Nancy. Since that time, the Zoo earned national accreditation and won both regional and national awards. 


Today, the 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization cooperates in conservation programs both in and outside the wild for endangered species. Naples Zoo was one of the first in the nation to include a 25 cent fee with each admission to fund conservation programs in the wild. Naples Zoo also plants a tree in Africa, Asia, or the Americas for each child visiting on a school field trip or guest attending a corporate event -- and even more trees for guests who become Zoo Members. 10% of the price of each stuffed plush predator or primate also funds conservation programs. Your visit makes a better world.

title: Gearlink Cup
description:
At the northern end of the Tampa Bay area, beautiful Pasco County is close to major cities but far from the hustle and bustle. Visit Pasco and enjoy Florida the way it used to be. Acres of pristine wilderness with biking, hiking and canoeing trails. Historic downtowns with fine restaurants and antique shops and dozens of family-oriented activities and sporting events year 'round. Pasco County is home to world-class tennis and golf resorts, including Saddlebrook Resort & Spa, one of Conde Nast Traveler's Top 100 and Lake Jovita, the Florida course that plays like North Carolina. 


Enjoy cultural treasures, such as the Historic Courthouse, built in 1909 in beautiful downtown Dade City and the Pioneer Florida Museum, home to period buildings dating to 1878. Experience historic walking tours of downtown New Port Richey, boat tours of the Pithlachascotee River and trolley tours in downtown Dade City. See the World War II Barracks Museum in Zephyrhills, the St. Leo Abbey & Grotto in St. Leo and an original "Cracker House'' in Holiday. Camp at Starkey Wilderness Park, cast your fishing line at Anclote River Park, paddle a kayak at Werner Boyce Salt Spring State Park. Hike the Suncoast Trail, visit spots along the Great Florida Birding Trail or charter a deep sea fishing excursion.


From the beaches on the Gulf Coast to scenic rivers like the Withlacoochee in the east to one of the world's premier drop zones at Skydive City, Pasco has something for everyone. See local and national acts perform at the Show Palace in Hudson and historic Richey Suncoast Theater in New Port Richey. Savor locally-made wines at the Florida Estates Winery in Land O' Lakes. Enjoy dozens of unique festivals, including Chasco Fiesta in New Port Richey and the Kumquat Festival in Dade City.

title: Performance Race Week
address: South Seas Island Resort - Captiva Island
city: Captiva Island and Ft Myers Beach FL
description:
Offshore Sailing School provides rewarding learning vacations at three premier SW Florida destination resorts. We give new meaning to fun-in-the-sun. Just want to try sailing? Learn how to make a boat move with wind alone? Pick any two days for a Learn to Sail or Learn to Cruise Adventure, or take a two-hour lesson. Gain Certification while you Learn to sail, cruise or race in three to five fun-filled days on the Gulf of Mexico or Tampa Bay.


Founded in 1964 by Olympic and America's Cup sailor, Steve Colgate, America's #1 Sailing School® also offers private and group lessons and sunset sails for vacationers already on site. Live aboard and shore based vacations include course and accommodations. Beginners and racers learn on award-winning Colgate 26 sailboats. Cruising courses are taught on state-of-the-art 43-49 foot cruising sailboats. Each day allows free time to enjoy other activities where you learn. Walk or drive Ding Darling National Refuge. Go to the Shell Museum. Fish, jog. bike, kayak, play tennis, enjoy a round of golf. Go shelling on long beautiful beaches, bask by gorgeous pools.    To learn more call 800-221-4326 or contact us on the web at  www.offshoresailing.com/contact.aspx  


Group and private programs available whether traveling alone, with a loved one, or the entire family. Private courses for two empower and build confidence. Singles make new friends while learning. These fun sailing adventures provide lasting skills and lifelong vacations under sail. As you sail and learn dolphins play in your wake and curious manatees circle as you dock.


Offshore Sailing School learning vacations and lessons are available at Pink Shell Beach Resort & Spa, Ft. Myers Beach; South Seas Island Resort, Captiva Island; and Mansion House B&B, St. Petersburg. Sailing is a green activity. It's fun and exhilarating to make a boat move with wind and sails alone. Reduce your carbon footprint every minute you're under sail. Sailing provides peace, freedom, inspiration and fun.


Call 800-221-4326 or contact us on the web at www.offshoresailing.com/contact.aspx


                                             Sailing—Good for You. Good for the World!(TM)

From the beaches on the Gulf Coast to scenic rivers like the Withlacoochee in the east to one of the world's premier drop zones at Skydive City, Pasco has something for everyone. See local and national acts perform at the Show Palace in Hudson and historic Richey Suncoast Theater in New Port Richey. Savor locally-made wines at the Florida Estates Winery in Land O' Lakes. Enjoy dozens of unique festivals, including Chasco Fiesta in New Port Richey and the Kumquat Festival in Dade City.

description: Bok Tower Gardens blends the beauty of nature, the intrigue of history and exceptional artistic and musical experiences to enrich the hearts and minds of all who visit. Enjoy Olmsted gardens, a majestic marble and coquina bell tower on one of peninsular Florida's highest points and daily 1 and 3 p.m. carillon concerts, Pinewood Estate's Mediterranean-style mansion and the Pine Ridge Nature Preserve. Visitor Center, Café and gift shop. National Historic Landmark near Lake Wales.

title: Music In The Park
description: Major Francis L. Dade spoke words of encouragement to 107 cold, tired soldiers in a pine forest on the morning of Dec. 28, 1835. Within eight hours, only three soldiers would survive the battle that marked the beginning of the Second Seminole War. The story of this momentous battle in Florida history is told in the visitor center at Dade Battlefield State Historic Site.

title: Old Time Dance
description: Located on the banks of the scenic and unique Santa Fe River, a tributary of the Suwannee River. Within O'Leno, the Santa Fe disappears and flows underground for more than three miles before it again becomes a surface stream at the River Rise. Fishing is allowed along the banks of the river (except in the swimming area) and in any of the many sinkhole ponds throughout the park. You may also launch a canoe (when the river is high enough) and fish upstream from the picnic area. Fish commonly caught are bass, brim and catfish.

title: 16th annual Giving Hunger the Blues concert and street festival
Riverwalk Get Downtown
description:
There was a time, not so long ago, when hospitality and service were expected to be an effortless part of the hotel experience. Guests were greeted with warm smiles from the moment they walked through the doors. Cocktails were served in the wood paneled bar, guests took breakfast on the patio, and dinner was an elegant affair. The Riverside has continued to uphold these fine standards. Since opening its doors in 1936, its name became synonymous with charm and elegance. And in the 72 years since, absolutely nothing has changed. Today, the Riverside Hotel remains a beacon of old world civility in a thriving, modern and beautiful destination, combining the highest levels of service with elegant accommodations, exquisite cuisine and prime location on the river in the heart of Fort Lauderdale’s downtown.
The Riverside is the city’s oldest hotel, built on the well-known Las Olas Boulevard dining and shopping district. An island in a sea of ultra modern skyscrapers, Las Olas offers a taste of Old Florida. It’s a place where professionals conduct business, whether dealing in local service or international markets. And it’s a place where travelers from across the globe come to discover the richness of South Florida. Situated on the banks of the New River, the Riverside Hotel is only blocks from Fort Lauderdale’s central business district. Guests can stroll the mile-long Riverwalk which leads from the pioneer Stranahan House to the acclaimed Broward Center for the Performing Arts, the Museum of Discovery and Science and IMAX Theater, the Fort Lauderdale Museum of Art, and the Broward County Main Library. The hotel is just minutes from the Fort Lauderdale/Hollywood International Airport, Port Everglades International Cruise Port and the Broward County Convention Center.
The Riverside Hotel can always be counted on for the quality, service and ambience of its unique and popular restaurants. Indigo restaurant serves traditional breakfast, lunch and dinner. The Grill Room on Las Olas is a Four Diamond AAA award recipient-for the ninth consecutive year, serves only the best quality seafood and meats complemented by an extensive wine list. The Golden Lyon Bar is a cozy gathering place where guests can enjoy cocktails and appetizers. Preston’s Lounge is located in the lobby where you can also enjoy cocktails, appetizers and great conversation.

title: Touch Tank and Coral Catshark Feeding
description:
A 2,000-square-foot public aquarium and ocean science education center at the Pier in downtown St. Petersburg. Touch Tank Tour Activity is scheduled 1-4 p.m. daily with Coral Catshark Feeding where visitors receive an "Official Shark Feeder" certificate for participating. A new first Saturday-of-the-month 2011 Book Nook by the Bay program scheduled 10:30am-noon features Fresh Fish Theater, our marine science  library, marine education and story time with guest authors and readers.


Exciting interactive exhibits, 14 aquariums housing fish and other critters particular to a specific ocean environment, educational fun activities & more! Newest exhibit: Coral Catshark Aquaculture Program showing life of a shark from egg to adult. Other exhibits by marine science partners spotlight their research, innovation and technology: Counting on Fish, a 352-gallon sport fish aquarium and a SmartPad touch screen, tells the story behind the importance of sport and commercial fish. Focus on Fish tells the story behind scientific illustration and features the work of St. Petersburg wildlife artist and illustrator Diane Rome Peebles.


Into the Eye: Hurricanes brings eye-opening information about hurricanes. A Sea of Sound brings the ocean chorus of burps, whistles, grunts, clucks and booms, a symphony of sound produced by fishes to life through our mobile hydrophone live feed installed underneath The Pier. Tampa Bay: Species of Concern addresses the issues about the manatee, the bay scallop, the loggerhead sea turtle and the Gulf Surgeon, all animals whose existence is closely monitored by researchers and environmental groups. Oceans: The Big Picture shows how satellites in space "see" very large areas and, since they stay in orbit around the Earth, continuously gather data about the same place.


Free outdoor exhibits: The Wonder of Water illustrates the water cycle on the walls of the Roy G. Harrell, Jr. Education Station and WaterWalk "kiosks" along the approach of The Pier give visitors a chance to learn about the body of water, Tampa Bay and the Gulf of Mexico, that surrounds them.


For adults only, four times a year we offer SciCafe St. Petersburg at a local restaurant. Past themes include: Caffeine May Be Good for You!; Nanotechnology: From Port Security to Sunscreen; Green Chemistry; A Sustainable Building: The Word is Photovoltaic, CSI Forensic Science: Fact or Fiction; Gulf Oil Spill; the Ocean and Human Health: The Good, the Bad, the Ugly.


Info: www.pieraquarium.com/scicafe

title: Safety Harbor Farmer\'s Market
description:
Safety Harbor is located by the sheltered inlets of Old Tampa Bay, on the “sunrise side of the bay” as the locals say.  Its colorful history includes Native American tribe headquarters, Spanish explorers, pirates, healing waters and the first grapefruit ever planted in Florida.


The community itself is welcoming and picturesque.  A beautiful waterfront park and marina offer excellent views of the bay as well as being a popular spot for viewing manatee in the summer months.  Next to the marina is the historic Safety Harbor Resort and Spa, a historical property situated on the site of ancient mineral springs once discovered by Spanish explorers in their quest for "the fountain of youth".  The mineral waters are still used today for spa treatments and drinking water.


Downtown Safety Harbor is definitely for walking.  Art galleries, shops, boutiques, a much-used pavilion and one of the largest live oak trees in existence can be found within several blocks.  The Chamber and welcome center provide brochures, visitor information and area gifts for purchase.  Restaurants and cafes abound; many are locally owned and offer outside dining.


The Safety Harbor Regional Museum of History offers a glimpse into the early development of the area and showcases artifacts, dioramas, and artwork dating to the 1500s.  The museum sits on the site of a Tocoboga Indian mound.


The very popular Philippe Park, a 122-acre county-run park, flanks scenic Tampa Bay and features scenic picnic shelters, playground, boat ramp and walking trails.  A raised Indian mound is on the site, as is the gravesite of Odet Philippe, whose land grant and subsequent developed citrus grove resulted in the first grapefruit ever planted in Florida.  Philippe has been inducted into the Florida Citrus Hall of Fame for his contributions to what is now a billion-dollar citrus industry in Florida.


For a small town with population under 20,000, Safety Harbor hosts many events throughout the year including the annual wine festival, HarbourSounds music festival and other family events.  On the third Friday of each month, the Main Street is closed down to street traffic and is lined with arts and crafts booths, food vendors, and entertainment.  A seasonal farmer's market is held by the pavilion throughout the cooler months.  Only 20 minutes from TPA and PIE airports and 30 minutes from Clearwater Beach, Safety Harbor is a perfect getaway.


.


The Safety Harbor Chamber of Commerce phone is (727)726-2890  www.safetyharbor.com

title: Original Log Homesite Guided Walk
description: Visitors to Dudley Farm Historic State Park will step back in time as they experience an original Florida pioneer living history farm established in the 1890s. Park staff in authentic farm clothing perform daily farm chores and encourage visitors to participate and 18 buildings still exist and include the Dudley family farmhouse and kitchen, the sugar cane mill and syrup house, the general store and post office. Pecan trees, fruit trees, vegetable and flower gardens, crop fields and woodlands comprise this 325-acre farm. The picnic areas and walking trails are available from the Visitor Center where a 12-minute video can be viewed. In 1983 Myrtle Dudley donated 25 acres of the farmstead to the Florida Park Service. By 2001 much of the building and landscape restoration had taken place, resulting in this National Register property opening to the public.

title: Friends of Fakahatchee Guided Boardwalk Tours
description: One of Florida's most spectacular natural landscapes. Visitors can experience what the park has to offer by hiking one of the numerous trails, taking a ranger-guided swampwalk or canoe or kayak tour, strolling the Big Cypress Bend Boardwalk or enjoying a leisurely trip down the 11-mile stretch of Jane's Scenic Drive. Fakahatchee Strand is the major drainage slough of southwestern Big Cypress Swamp. The forests of bald cypresses are as impressive as any in the state. It contains the largest stand of native royal palms and the largest concentration and variety of epiphytic orchids in North America.

title: Corporate Sail-Race Challenge
address: South Seas Island Resort - Captiva Island
city: Captiva Island and Ft Myers Beach FL
description:
Offshore Sailing School provides rewarding learning vacations at three premier SW Florida destination resorts. We give new meaning to fun-in-the-sun. Just want to try sailing? Learn how to make a boat move with wind alone? Pick any two days for a Learn to Sail or Learn to Cruise Adventure, or take a two-hour lesson. Gain Certification while you Learn to sail, cruise or race in three to five fun-filled days on the Gulf of Mexico or Tampa Bay.


Founded in 1964 by Olympic and America's Cup sailor, Steve Colgate, America's #1 Sailing School® also offers private and group lessons and sunset sails for vacationers already on site. Live aboard and shore based vacations include course and accommodations. Beginners and racers learn on award-winning Colgate 26 sailboats. Cruising courses are taught on state-of-the-art 43-49 foot cruising sailboats. Each day allows free time to enjoy other activities where you learn. Walk or drive Ding Darling National Refuge. Go to the Shell Museum. Fish, jog. bike, kayak, play tennis, enjoy a round of golf. Go shelling on long beautiful beaches, bask by gorgeous pools.    To learn more call 800-221-4326 or contact us on the web at  www.offshoresailing.com/contact.aspx  


Group and private programs available whether traveling alone, with a loved one, or the entire family. Private courses for two empower and build confidence. Singles make new friends while learning. These fun sailing adventures provide lasting skills and lifelong vacations under sail. As you sail and learn dolphins play in your wake and curious manatees circle as you dock.


Offshore Sailing School learning vacations and lessons are available at Pink Shell Beach Resort & Spa, Ft. Myers Beach; South Seas Island Resort, Captiva Island; and Mansion House B&B, St. Petersburg. Sailing is a green activity. It's fun and exhilarating to make a boat move with wind and sails alone. Reduce your carbon footprint every minute you're under sail. Sailing provides peace, freedom, inspiration and fun.


Call 800-221-4326 or contact us on the web at www.offshoresailing.com/contact.aspx

title: Ghost Walk
description: Settled in 1894, this religious settlement boasted 50 buildings at one time, 11 of which still remain, including the Bakery, Art Hall and the restored home of founder Cyrus Reed Teed. The College of Life Foundation across street maintains archives. A nationally recognized historical site, Koreshan State Historic Site was a utopian community. Fishing, camping, nature study, picnicking, playground, boat ramp and canoes for rent. Guided walks and campfire programs seasonally.

title: HORSEMANSHIP (semi-annually)
address: A1A, 7 miles north of Little Talbot
description: Offering more than 200 acres of undeveloped sea island recreational opportunities. This is a perfect place to relax and unwind, search for seashells or see some rare wildlife. At Amelia Island State Park you can go horseback riding on the beach with Kelly Seahorse Ranch or gain access to the George Crady Bridge Fishing Pier State Park.

title: Guided Mountain Bike Ride
description: With unique topography that offers some of the most radical elevation changes in Florida, the Alafia off-road bicycling trails are the most challenging in the area. There are three major loops. Black Loop is very technical with steep drops and strenuous climbs and is for the advanced rider. Blue Loop, requires the skills of an intermediate rider on short sections. Green Loop, the easiest of the trails, but still challenging, for experienced beginners. Helmets are required on ALL bike trails.

title: Ranger-Guided Nature Walk
description: This park is made up of a group of islands in the Middle Keys, with public access to swimming, a playground, picnic tables, grills and showers on the ocean side of Little Crawl Key. Open for camping year round. Reservations are available through Reserve America. The park is open for day use year-round. Pets are not allowed on the beach or in the water. The park does not have a boat launch or a parking area for boat trailers, most park waters are a no-motor zone. Kayak rentals are available at the ranger station.

title: Star Party - Call for dates
description: One of the few state parks with dry (air filled) caves and the only Florida state park to offer cave tours to the public. The cave has dazzling formations of limestone stalactites, stalagmites, soda straws, flowstones and draperies. Florida Caverns is also popular for camping, swimming, fishing, picnicking, canoeing, boating, hiking, bicycling and horseback riding. Though the park does not rent horses, stables are available for equestrian campers. Cave tours last approximately 45 minutes and are considered to be moderately strenuous. An audiovisual program about the cave tour and the park is available in the visitor center. ***PLEASE NOTE*** Cave tours are CLOSED on Tuesdays and Wednesdays each week.

description: This island is a seasonal host for many of the nation's most prominent fishermen, as well as some of the most prominent families in the country. They come to fish for tarpon in Boca Grande pass, which separates Gasparilla and Cayo Costa islands. Each spring these giant fish, known also as "silver kings" migrate into the deep water pass, also known as the "Tarpon Capital of the World." Also located in the park is the Boca Grande Lighthouse Museum.

title: Prairie Buggy Tours
description: The Kilpatrick Hammock Campground at Kissimmee Prairie Preserve State Park offers 20 beautiful, shady sites with electric, water and dump station and 15 equestrian sites for horseback campers. A spacious bathhouse with clean showers and laundry facilities is available in the family camping area. Horse paddocks are available at the equestrian campground. Early morning and late evening, local wildlife such as white-tailed deer and turkey are often seen meandering through the camping areas.

title: 1876 Cow Camp
description: "Something for every visitor," including access to Florida's third largest lake, shaded camping and picnic facilities. Excellent wildlife viewing opportunities, beautiful nature trails for hiking, biking and horseback riding and a genuine 1876 "Cow Camp".

title: Tomoka Remembers
description: Located near the confluence of the Tomoka and Halifax rivers, Tomoka State Park offers scenic oaks and camping where early Native Americans once lived off the fish-filled lagoons. Camping, canoeing, fishing, boating, picnicking and nature trails are available. Swimming is not permitted in the rivers within this park.

title: GreenLinks rebrands to focus on Golf Travelers
venue: GreenLinks Golf Villas at Lely Resort
description: Located on two championship golf courses in Naples, FL, GreenLinks Golf Villas at Lely Resort is a great  location for a relaxing vacation. Inside the stunning Lely Resort , GreenLinks Golf Villas blends a resort experience with a residential lifestyle. GreenLinks offers nightly & weekly rentals of 200 beautifully appointed two- and three-bedroom Villas. Amenities include: tennis courts, heated pool, gas barbeque grills, whirlpool spa, the Flamingo Island Grille Restaurant & Lounge and pro shop. Guests can experience Naples’ only Robert Trent Jones, Sr. signature course, Lely Flamingo Golf Course or Lee Trevino’s intensely designed Lely Mustang course. Close by you have horseback riding in the Picayune State Forest, kayaking in Rookery Bay Natural Estuarine Research Reserve, off trail biking in Collier Seminole State Forest, backwater fishing in the 10,000 Islands, bird watching in Big Cypress National preserve or J.N. "Ding" Darling National Wildlife refuge, watch alligators as you bike through Shark Valley in Everglades National Park, shoot sporting clays at Port of the Islands Gun Club, motorcycle up and down the West Coast of Florida in a rented Harley. On the gentler side are spa treatments at the on-site Players Club & Spa. Walking through the neighborhoods here at Lely Resort or sitting by the pool with a good read are two addtional options. Rent bicycles and explore the resort as well. Parents will appreaciate the board games, dvd movies, tennis equipment and beach accessories available at the front desk at no charge. Come enjoy the GreenLinks experience! Check our website for packages!!!

title: St. Josoph History Tour
description: The monument was erected in 1922 and bears the names of the convention delegates engraved in marble. The vast landscape boasts a promenade of palm trees that escort you from the monument to the water's edge. One of the most picturesque parks in Gulf County, this location is proven ideal for social gatherings, weddings and festivals. Local history and self-guided museum for the drafting of a state constitution and Port St. Joe.

title: Delicate Balance of Nature - Lecture Series
venue: Dagny Johnson Key Largo Hammock Botanical State Park
description: This site includes the largest contiguous tract of subtropical West Indian hardwood hammock still found in the continental United States. These parklands were set-aside as an area of critical concern and are home to 84 protected species of plants and animals.

title: Saturday Ranger Walk
description: A stairway descends from the rim of this 120-foot-deep sinkhole into a miniature rain forest. This huge sinkhole was formed when an underground cavern roof collapsed. Small streams tumble down the steep slopes of the sink, disappearing through crevices at the bottom. The lush growth of plants and many of the animals of the park are similar to those of the Appalachian Mountains region. The sinkhole may be explored from the boardwalks and stairways.

title: Wesley House Guided Tours
description:
Was once the home of the William Henry Wesley family, is now a place of tranquility and contemplation. Yet, nearly 100 years ago, a visit to Eden Gardens State Park would have vibrated with the whir of mechanical and human energy.  Originally the site of a sawmill, it is now a gorgeous park that features guided tours of the Wesley House.  Experience the elegance of Louis XVI furniture as well as other periods in the park's renovated two-story house, originally built in 1897.

Come wander our formal ornamental gardens and enjoy camellias, azaleas, Heritage Roses, daylilies depending upon the season.  Enjoy the reflection pond and the koi, take time to wander in the Hidden Garden and discover it's secrets!

We have picnic areas as well, so come spend an hour or spend the day, you are welcome at Eden!

title: Hammock Walk
description: The shores and coastal waters at this park provide an abundance of recreational opportunities. The breathtaking beautiful half-mile beach welcomes visitors for swimming, snorkeling, surfing and scuba diving. Beachcombing, picnicking or just relaxing on the sand are also popular activities. Dynamite Point was once the training site for WWII Navy Frogmen, but is now a haven for birdwatchers. Along the south end of the park, Fort Pierce Inlet is a popular place for anglers to catch dinner.

title: Ardisia Days

description: Named for an old Spanish Mission, San Francisco de Potano which ministered to the Indians living here centuries ago. Over time the early settlers continually mispronounced San Francisco until the area became known as San Felasco. "Hammock" is an Indian word that means "shady." The lower two thirds of San Felasco has been set aside for hiking only. The northern most 2,000 acres have been designated for multi-use purposes including horseback riding, off-road bicycling and hiking.

Picnic tables are available near the center. Guided walks and canoe trips are available by reservation.

Naturalist led kayak and bike ecotours through State Parks in Jacksonville/Amelia Island area. Get answers to questions like "Why do mullet jump?" and "Why is that crab waving at me?" No experience needed, all tours start with a short paddling instruction.       


Bike ecotours traverse the flat trails through Talbot & Ft Clinch State Parks and Guana Reserve. Under the Oak canopy you will learn about the uplands habitat. Home to raccoons, armadillos, deer, hawks and owls to name but a few.

New program offers eco-teambuilding for businesses and groups. description: The Tallahassee Museum is located on 52 acres of scenic woodlands in Southwest Tallahassee bordering beautiful Lake Bradford. The city's oldest museum chronicles the history and heritage of north Florida and south Georgia. title: Florida Folk Festival
description: Jewel of the Suwannee Set amid the lush greenery, winding waterways and native wilderness, North Florida is one of the Sunshine State's little known and most precious treasures.  Cut from nature's flawless beauty and set apart by a band of shimmering waters, this sparkling gem reflects the many colorful facets of Florida's rich history and original unspoiled splendor.  It is here in crystal-clear waters, under sapphire skies and golden sun, shaded by an emerald canopy of green that visitors discover Hamilton County, Florida - the "Jewel of the Suwannee".Resting on the Florida-Georgia border, Hamilton County is truely set apart from the rest of the state.  Bordered by the Withlacoochee River to the west and the World Famous Suwannee River to the east and south, the county forms a penisula within a penisula, uniquely separated from the landmass of Florida.  Neatly splitting this river county is the twisting Alapaha River, adding to the vitality and beauty of a paradise for nature lovers and outdoor sports enthusiasts for all ages.  The protected waters of Hamilton County's rivers, crystal clear springs and numberous lakes provide endless opportunities for outdoor activities.  Whether camping, hunting, photography or just exploring by foot, bike, horseback, canoe or kayak, you'll find it to be the "Jewel of the Suwannee".  A Tale of Two Treasures  While Hamilton County is undeniably a natural treasure, it is equally valuable as one of Florida's historic treasures.  With more than 150 sites and structures on the National Register of Historic Places, Hamilton County is a popular destination for both casual history buffs and the more serious genealogy researchers, the county is landscaped with more than 50 county cemeteries, including what is believed to be Florida's oldest.  For those who will listen, these weathered tombstones and grave markers just may whisper a tale.Hamilton County, better known as the "Jewel of the Suwannee" says, "come for a visit, stay for a lifetime".  While visiting Hamilton Couty , we invite you to visit the 888-acre Stephen Foster Folk Culture Center State Park in quaint White Springs - home to the first hub of the Suwannee River Wilderness Trail and Florida Trail.

title: Early Bird Special
description:
A hidden gem located in the "Nature Coast" of Florida on the Gulf of Mexico, our beautiful eco-friendly and  green lodging resort is surrounded by the natural springs of King's Bay in Crystal River and home to over 400 West Indian Manatee who migrate each winter to the constant 72 degree springs and to the only place in the Country where you can legally swim with these gentle giants.


The resort rests on 232 acres of lush greens, emerald pines and grand oaks is manicured with great precision.  Our196 well appointed and spacious guest rooms and suites which include 12 two story golf villas with a spectacular view of the golf course offer the comfort of true hospitality and a tranquil experience.


Our Marina and Dive Shop offers great water activities, boat rentals, kayak rentals, canoe rentals, guided river tours, scuba diving tours, PADI certification and Manatee snorkel tours during the peak season from October to March,  we do have year round Manatee residence but recommend tours during peak winter months.  


The finest of Florida golf rave our golf enthusiasts who travel to conquer our Mark Mahannah designed 18 holes championship course; you can mix and match our three nines to suit your particular strength or weakness.  If it’s a short course you prefer, our 9 hole Lagoons course and is a great option to sharpen your short game.  Our links are beautifully manicured and well groomed; the course has a variety of water and bunker obstacles.  The course has aged well and offers an assortment of challenging fairways lined with mature emerald pines, grand oaks and is home to much wildlife.


Our full service Aveda Spa offers; hair, nail and skincare services as well as couples massage room with a working fireplace and a perfect setting for a romantic getaway or that honeymoon that you never took.


We have a lagoon style heated swimming pool and a Jacuzzi overlooking the beautiful river; we offer our guests food and beverage service from our Tiki bar which is open seasonally. 


The Plantation Room is our main dining room and offers breakfast, lunch and dinner service, we also have a Library bar a great central gathering place, our Tiki bar is open seasonally and is well attended by guests and neighbors who can pull up their boat and enjoy our great culinary fare and the beautiful Florida sunshine.  Our Pro-Bar offers a great menu for those golfers who want a quick burger or our wonderful members who enjoy a great sandwich, cold beverage a perfect view of the golf course.

title: Spring Camp
description:
DEERING ESTATE AT CUTLER
Located along the edge of Biscayne Bay, the 444-acre Deering Estate at Cutler is an environmental, archeological and historical preserve. From canoe rides to butterfly hikes, and nature guided tours, the Deering Estate has diverse activities for the whole family to enjoy. The Estate offers daily tours of the historic houses – the Stone House and Richmond Cottage, as well as naturalist lead tours of the lush natural areas where fossil bones have been found as far back at 50,000 years. title: Fort Cooper Days
description:
The park is named for Major Mark Anthony Cooper, commander of 380 First Georgia Battalion Volunteers plus an artillery company of a few army regulars. In April 1836 Major Mark Anthony Cooper built a fort near the lake's edge to protect the sick and wounded left behind by General Scott as he continued on his way to Fort Brooke, which is now Tampa. Major Cooper was ordered to hold his position and await relief troops in nine days. By the third day the Seminoles, led by Osceola and other Chiefs, discovered Major Cooper and his men. They kept them under constant daily attacks. On one occasion the Seminoles tried to storm the fort with a force in "excess of 500 warriors." After 16 days, with provisions running out, the troops in the fort were saved when a relief column returned to support them.

Due to Major Cooper's vigilant leadership during the two week siege, the Georgia Battalion sustained about 20 men wounded, but lost only one man. It is unknown how many casualties were taken by the Seminole warriors. Fort Cooper was utilized as a reconnaissance, observation and dispatch post until 1842 by various U.S. Army detachments.

The park's diverse natural areas provide a refuge for many plants and animals. The inland woods feature hammocks of hickory, oak, magnolia and sweet gum. Beyond is the sandhill community, a dry, open forest of long leaf pines and turkey oaks. Sightings of deer, turkey, opossum and bobcat are common. Owls, herons and cardinals are frequently seen in the park.

At the northern end of the Tampa Bay area, beautiful Pasco County is close to major cities but far from the hustle and bustle. Visit Pasco and enjoy Florida the way it used to be. Acres of pristine wilderness with biking, hiking and canoeing trails. Historic downtowns with fine restaurants and antique shops and dozens of family-oriented activities and sporting events year 'round. Pasco County is home to world-class tennis and golf resorts, including Saddlebrook Resort & Spa, one of Conde Nast Traveler's Top 100 and Lake Jovita, the Florida course that plays like North Carolina. 


Enjoy cultural treasures, such as the Historic Courthouse, built in 1909 in beautiful downtown Dade City and the Pioneer Florida Museum, home to period buildings dating to 1878. Experience historic walking tours of downtown New Port Richey, boat tours of the Pithlachascotee River and trolley tours in downtown Dade City. See the World War II Barracks Museum in Zephyrhills, the St. Leo Abbey & Grotto in St. Leo and an original "Cracker House'' in Holiday. From the beaches on the Gulf Coast to scenic rivers like the Withlacoochee in the east to one of the world's premier drop zones at Skydive City, Pasco has something for everyone. See local and national acts perform at the Show Palace in Hudson and historic Richey Suncoast Theater in New Port Richey. Savor locally-made wines at the Florida Estates Winery in Land O' Lakes. Enjoy dozens of unique festivals, including Chasco Fiesta in New Port Richey and the Kumquat Festival in Dade City.

title: Annual Golf Tournament
Wld Azalea Festival
description: Jewel of the Suwannee Set amid the lush greenery, winding waterways and native wilderness, North Florida is one of the Sunshine State's little known and most precious treasures.  Cut from nature's flawless beauty and set apart by a band of shimmering waters, this sparkling gem reflects the many colorful facets of Florida's rich history and original unspoiled splendor.  It is here in crystal-clear waters, under sapphire skies and golden sun, shaded by an emerald canopy of green that visitors discover Hamilton County, Florida - the "Jewel of the Suwannee".Resting on the Florida-Georgia border, Hamilton County is truely set apart from the rest of the state.  Bordered by the Withlacoochee River to the west and the World Famous Suwannee River to the east and south, the county forms a penisula within a penisula, uniquely separated from the landmass of Florida.  Neatly splitting this river county is the twisting Alapaha River, adding to the vitality and beauty of a paradise for nature lovers and outdoor sports enthusiasts for all ages.  The protected waters of Hamilton County's rivers, crystal clear springs and numberous lakes provide endless opportunities for outdoor activities.  Whether camping, hunting, photography or just exploring by foot, bike, horseback, canoe or kayak, you'll find it to be the "Jewel of the Suwannee".  A Tale of Two Treasures  While Hamilton County is undeniably a natural treasure, it is equally valuable as one of Florida's historic treasures.  With more than 150 sites and structures on the National Register of Historic Places, Hamilton County is a popular destination for both casual history buffs and the more serious genealogy researchers, the county is landscaped with more than 50 county cemeteries, including what is believed to be Florida's oldest.  For those who will listen, these weathered tombstones and grave markers just may whisper a tale.Hamilton County, better known as the "Jewel of the Suwannee" says, "come for a visit, stay for a lifetime".  While visiting Hamilton Couty , we invite you to visit the 888-acre Stephen Foster Folk Culture Center State Park in quaint White Springs - home to the first hub of the Suwannee River Wilderness Trail and Florida Trail.

venue: Central Florida Zoo and Botanical Gardens
description:
Enter the enchanted, tropical world of the Central Florida Zoo & Botanical Gardens, a relaxing, entertaining and educational experience for the entire family. You’ll discover a world of animals from around the world within this tropical park nestled in the heart of Florida. Stroll along shaded, winding boardwalks and paths as you see towering elephants, search for the elusive cheetah, appreciate the beauty of the hyacinth macaw and listen to the song of the kookaburra. Hop on over to the Horizon Homes of Central Florida Australia exhibit featuring emus and kangaroos or dare to meet some of the world’s most venomous reptiles and non-venomous snakes, lizards and frogs in the Herpetarium. Feed goats, sheep, llamas, zebus, and other domestic animals in the Animal Adventure area. Don’t miss the native wildlife that resides in the lush, tropical setting of the Zoo.

There's always something new to see at the Zoo including the recently opened Wharton-Smith Tropical Splash Ground! So bring your swimsuit and flip-flops and jump in to cool off.  Afterwards, take a peek at the endangered Amur leopards, the venomous king cobra, the slow sloth and watch the siamangs, king vultures and cougar enjoy habitats to swing, fly and relax. The Butterfly Sensory Garden incorporates touch, look, listen and smell stations to show how insect senses differ from those of humans in addition to the many plant varieties featured to attract and support all stages of the butterfly or take a ride on Champ the Train or a spin on the Animal Carousel.

Among the most popular programs is the up-close and personal Animal Encounters on weekends and holidays, in which docents educate visitors about the characteristics of animals from alligators to hedgehogs to snakes. Other popular weekend programs include an elephant demonstration, bird training, and feeding programs for felines and primates. Behind-the-Scenes Elephant Encounters offer visitors a once-in-a-lifetime experience to feed and touch the Asian elephants.

With something for everyone, the adventures are endless!

address: 15 Fort Mose Trl., off of U.S. 1 North
description: The first free African settlement in North America and a premier site on the Florida Black Heritage trail. description:
DEERING ESTATE AT CUTLER
Located along the edge of Biscayne Bay, the 444-acre Deering Estate at Cutler is an environmental, archeological and historical preserve. From canoe rides to butterfly hikes, and nature guided tours, the Deering Estate has diverse activities for the whole family to enjoy. The Estate offers daily tours of the historic houses – the Stone House and Richmond Cottage, as well as naturalist lead tours of the lush natural areas where fossil bones have been found as far back at 50,000 years. The Estate is part of the Miami-Dade County Park and Recreation Department, which manages the Estate on behalf of the State of Florida. 

The Deering Estate is also a cultural and educational facility that features classes and programs for children and adults, teacher training and research opportunities. The Estate also serves as a small conference center for community organizations and corporate groups who share Charles Deering’s interest in the environment, botany, history, fine arts, antiques, rare books and wine. Rental of the Estate is available for special social functions. General admission includes tours of the historic homes and natural areas. Special eco-tours and guided canoe trips to the offshore island of Chicken Key are available for an additional fee. 16701 SW 72 Ave, Miami, FL 33157, 305-235-1668. www.deeringestate.org.

description: Jewel of the Suwannee Set amid the lush greenery, winding waterways and native wilderness, North Florida is one of the Sunshine State's little known and most precious treasures.  Cut from nature's flawless beauty and set apart by a band of shimmering waters, this sparkling gem reflects the many colorful facets of Florida's rich history and original unspoiled splendor.  It is here in crystal-clear waters, under sapphire skies and golden sun, shaded by an emerald canopy of green that visitors discover Hamilton County, Florida - the "Jewel of the Suwannee".Resting on the Florida-Georgia border, Hamilton County is truely set apart from the rest of the state.  Bordered by the Withlacoochee River to the west and the World Famous Suwannee River to the east and south, the county forms a penisula within a penisula, uniquely separated from the landmass of Florida.  Neatly splitting this river county is the twisting Alapaha River, adding to the vitality and beauty of a paradise for nature lovers and outdoor sports enthusiasts for all ages.  The protected waters of Hamilton County's rivers, crystal clear springs and numberous lakes provide endless opportunities for outdoor activities.  Whether camping, hunting, photography or just exploring by foot, bike, horseback, canoe or kayak, you'll find it to be the "Jewel of the Suwannee".  A Tale of Two Treasures  While Hamilton County is undeniably a natural treasure, it is equally valuable as one of Florida's historic treasures.  With more than 150 sites and structures on the National Register of Historic Places, Hamilton County is a popular destination for both casual history buffs and the more serious genealogy researchers, the county is landscaped with more than 50 county cemeteries, including what is believed to be Florida's oldest.  For those who will listen, these weathered tombstones and grave markers just may whisper a tale.Hamilton County, better known as the "Jewel of the Suwannee" says, "come for a visit, stay for a lifetime".  While visiting Hamilton Couty , we invite you to visit the 888-acre Stephen Foster Folk Culture Center State Park in quaint White Springs - home to the first hub of the Suwannee River Wilderness Trail and Florida Trail.

title: April 2 Book Nook by the Bay
description:
A 2,000-square-foot public aquarium and ocean science education center at the Pier in downtown St. Petersburg. Touch Tank Tour Activity is scheduled 1-4 p.m. daily with Coral Catshark Feeding where visitors receive an "Official Shark Feeder" certificate for participating. A new first Saturday-of-the-month 2011 Book Nook by the Bay program scheduled 10:30am-noon features Fresh Fish Theater, our marine science  library, marine education and story time with guest authors and readers.


Exciting interactive exhibits, 14 aquariums housing fish and other critters particular to a specific ocean environment, educational fun activities & more! Newest exhibit: Coral Catshark Aquaculture Program showing life of a shark from egg to adult. Other exhibits by marine science partners spotlight their research, innovation and technology: Counting on Fish, a 352-gallon sport fish aquarium and a SmartPad touch screen, tells the story behind the importance of sport and commercial fish. Focus on Fish tells the story behind scientific illustration and features the work of St. Petersburg wildlife artist and illustrator Diane Rome Peebles.


Into the Eye: Hurricanes brings eye-opening information about hurricanes. A Sea of Sound brings the ocean chorus of burps, whistles, grunts, clucks and booms, a symphony of sound produced by fishes to life through our mobile hydrophone live feed installed underneath The Pier. Tampa Bay: Species of Concern addresses the issues about the manatee, the bay scallop, the loggerhead sea turtle and the Gulf Surgeon, all animals whose existence is closely monitored by researchers and environmental groups. Oceans: The Big Picture shows how satellites in space "see" very large areas and, since they stay in orbit around the Earth, continuously gather data about the same place.


Free outdoor exhibits: The Wonder of Water illustrates the water cycle on the walls of the Roy G. Harrell, Jr. Education Station and WaterWalk "kiosks" along the approach of The Pier give visitors a chance to learn about the body of water, Tampa Bay and the Gulf of Mexico, that surrounds them.


For adults only, four times a year we offer SciCafe St. Petersburg at a local restaurant. Past themes include: Caffeine May Be Good for You!; Nanotechnology: From Port Security to Sunscreen; Green Chemistry; A Sustainable Building: The Word is Photovoltaic, CSI Forensic Science: Fact or Fiction; Gulf Oil Spill; the Ocean and Human Health: The Good, the Bad, the Ugly.

title: Storytime at the Zoo
venue: Central Florida Zoo and Botanical Gardens
description:
Enter the enchanted, tropical world of the Central Florida Zoo & Botanical Gardens, a relaxing, entertaining and educational experience for the entire family. You’ll discover a world of animals from around the world within this tropical park nestled in the heart of Florida. Stroll along shaded, winding boardwalks and paths as you see towering elephants, search for the elusive cheetah, appreciate the beauty of the hyacinth macaw and listen to the song of the kookaburra. Hop on over to the Horizon Homes of Central Florida Australia exhibit featuring emus and kangaroos or dare to meet some of the world’s most venomous reptiles and non-venomous snakes, lizards and frogs in the Herpetarium. Feed goats, sheep, llamas, zebus, and other domestic animals in the Animal Adventure area. Don’t miss the native wildlife that resides in the lush, tropical setting of the Zoo.

There's always something new to see at the Zoo including the recently opened Wharton-Smith Tropical Splash Ground! So bring your swimsuit and flip-flops and jump in to cool off.  Afterwards, take a peek at the endangered Amur leopards, the venomous king cobra, the slow sloth and watch the siamangs, king vultures and cougar enjoy habitats to swing, fly and relax. The Butterfly Sensory Garden incorporates touch, look, listen and smell stations to show how insect senses differ from those of humans in addition to the many plant varieties featured to attract and support all stages of the butterfly or take a ride on Champ the Train or a spin on the Animal Carousel.

Among the most popular programs is the up-close and personal Animal Encounters on weekends and holidays, in which docents educate visitors about the characteristics of animals from alligators to hedgehogs to snakes. Other popular weekend programs include an elephant demonstration, bird training, and feeding programs for felines and primates. Behind-the-Scenes Elephant Encounters offer visitors a once-in-a-lifetime experience to feed and touch the Asian elephants.

With something for everyone, the adventures are endless!

title: The Barnacle Under Moonlight - Solar Dogs
description: This beautiful house with a whimsical name dates to a quieter time. The Barnacle, built in 1891, offers a glimpse of Old Florida during "The Era of the Bay." Situated on the shore of Biscayne Bay, this was the home of Ralph Middleton Munroe, one of Coconut Grove’s most charming and influential pioneers. Munroe’s principal passion was designing yachts. In his lifetime, he drew plans for 56 different sailboats. As a seaman, naturalist and photographer, Commodore Munroe was a man who cherished the natural world around him. A walk into the park passes through a tropical hardwood hammock. In the 1920s, it was representative of the original landscape within the city of Miami. Today, it is one of the last remnants of the once vast "Miami Hammock." Visitors enjoy sitting on rocking chairs on the spacious porch used as a gathering place or on a bench under a tree for solitude.

title: Fort Lauderdale International Car Show
description:
There was a time, not so long ago, when hospitality and service were expected to be an effortless part of the hotel experience. Guests were greeted with warm smiles from the moment they walked through the doors. Cocktails were served in the wood paneled bar, guests took breakfast on the patio, and dinner was an elegant affair. The Riverside has continued to uphold these fine standards. Since opening its doors in 1936, its name became synonymous with charm and elegance. And in the 72 years since, absolutely nothing has changed. Today, the Riverside Hotel remains a beacon of old world civility in a thriving, modern and beautiful destination, combining the highest levels of service with elegant accommodations, exquisite cuisine and prime location on the river in the heart of Fort Lauderdale’s downtown.
The Riverside is the city’s oldest hotel, built on the well-known Las Olas Boulevard dining and shopping district. An island in a sea of ultra modern skyscrapers, Las Olas offers a taste of Old Florida. It’s a place where professionals conduct business, whether dealing in local service or international markets. And it’s a place where travelers from across the globe come to discover the richness of South Florida. Situated on the banks of the New River, the Riverside Hotel is only blocks from Fort Lauderdale’s central business district. Guests can stroll the mile-long Riverwalk which leads from the pioneer Stranahan House to the acclaimed Broward Center for the Performing Arts, the Museum of Discovery and Science and IMAX Theater, the Fort Lauderdale Museum of Art, and the Broward County Main Library. The hotel is just minutes from the Fort Lauderdale/Hollywood International Airport, Port Everglades International Cruise Port and the Broward County Convention Center.
The Riverside Hotel can always be counted on for the quality, service and ambience of its unique and popular restaurants. Indigo restaurant serves traditional breakfast, lunch and dinner. The Grill Room on Las Olas is a Four Diamond AAA award recipient-for the ninth consecutive year, serves only the best quality seafood and meats complemented by an extensive wine list. The Golden Lyon Bar is a cozy gathering place where guests can enjoy cocktails and appetizers. Preston’s Lounge is located in the lobby where you can also enjoy cocktails, appetizers and great conversation.

title: Party on the Pass
description:
Ocean adventures await year ’round at Mote Aquarium, home to more than 100 marine species and exhibits showcasing the adjoining Mote Marine Laboratory. See freaky frogfish, huge scuttling lobsters and other denizens of Southwest Florida’s Gulf Coast, including sandbar, nurse, blacknose and bonnethead sharks. Guests can also see dolphins, manatees and sea turtles.

At our brand new exhibit, the Seahorse Conservation Laboratory, you can see graceful seahorses and their tiny young, or fry. You can learn about the threats wild seahorses face and watch Mote aquarists raise these fragile fish. Guests might even witness a little seahorse romance or spot a pregnant dad (that's right — male seahorses are the only animal dads that carry young in a belly pouch). 

At our new exhibit Sea Turtles: Ancient Survivors, visitors can learn how sea turtles outlived the dinosaurs and how these animals need our help to survive in modern times. An interactive display even lets you follow the journey of real sea turtles tagged in the wild by Mote scientists and see where they went between feeding and breeding seasons.

If you want to dive deeper into ocean fun, try our new "Breakfast at Mote" tours. These group tours allow small groups to enjoy Mote’s facilities before we open our doors to the general public. Participants can linger in front of their favorite exhibits, take unobstructed photos and even see bits of our morning routine, from fish feedings to shark tank cleanings. Your admission includes a continental breakfast and guided Aquarium tour. Ticket prices are $23 per person ($11 for Mote members). Go to www.mote.org/breakfast for more info.

When you buy a ticket to Mote Aquarium, you support world-renowned research at Mote Marine Laboratory. Visitors can glimpse our cutting-edge science and learn about the lab’s founding director, Eugenie Clark, and the research she did when the lab opened its doors in 1955. You can also see the work she and other researchers are doing at Mote today.

Mote Aquarium is open from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. 365 days a year at 1600 Ken Thompson Parkway, City Island, Sarasota. Admission prices are $17 for adults, $16 for seniors and $12 for kids ages 4-12. Mote Members and kids 3 and younger always get in free.

description:
Enter the enchanted, tropical world of the Central Florida Zoo & Botanical Gardens, a relaxing, entertaining and educational experience for the entire family. You’ll discover a world of animals from around the world within this tropical park nestled in the heart of Florida. Stroll along shaded, winding boardwalks and paths as you see towering elephants, search for the elusive cheetah, appreciate the beauty of the hyacinth macaw and listen to the song of the kookaburra. Hop on over to the Horizon Homes of Central Florida Australia exhibit featuring emus and kangaroos or dare to meet some of the world’s most venomous reptiles and non-venomous snakes, lizards and frogs in the Herpetarium. Feed goats, sheep, llamas, zebus, and other domestic animals in the Animal Adventure area. Don’t miss the native wildlife that resides in the lush, tropical setting of the Zoo.

There's always something new to see at the Zoo including the recently opened Wharton-Smith Tropical Splash Ground! So bring your swimsuit and flip-flops and jump in to cool off.  Afterwards, take a peek at the endangered Amur leopards, the venomous king cobra, the slow sloth and watch the siamangs, king vultures and cougar enjoy habitats to swing, fly and relax. The Butterfly Sensory Garden incorporates touch, look, listen and smell stations to show how insect senses differ from those of humans in addition to the many plant varieties featured to attract and support all stages of the butterfly or take a ride on Champ the Train or a spin on the Animal Carousel.

Among the most popular programs is the up-close and personal Animal Encounters on weekends and holidays, in which docents educate visitors about the characteristics of animals from alligators to hedgehogs to snakes. Other popular weekend programs include an elephant demonstration, bird training, and feeding programs for felines and primates. Behind-the-Scenes Elephant Encounters offer visitors a once-in-a-lifetime experience to feed and touch the Asian elephants.

With something for everyone, the adventures are endless!
