title: 2nd Annual FGA Geo-Extravaganza
description:
At the northern end of the Tampa Bay area, beautiful Pasco County is close to major cities but far from the hustle and bustle. Visit Pasco and enjoy Florida the way it used to be. Acres of pristine wilderness with biking, hiking and canoeing trails. Historic downtowns with fine restaurants and antique shops and dozens of family-oriented activities and sporting events year 'round. Pasco County is home to world-class tennis and golf resorts, including Saddlebrook Resort & Spa, one of Conde Nast Traveler's Top 100 and Lake Jovita, the Florida course that plays like North Carolina. 


Enjoy cultural treasures, such as the Historic Courthouse, built in 1909 in beautiful downtown Dade City and the Pioneer Florida Museum, home to period buildings dating to 1878. Experience historic walking tours of downtown New Port Richey, boat tours of the Pithlachascotee River and trolley tours in downtown Dade City. See the World War II Barracks Museum in Zephyrhills, the St. Leo Abbey & Grotto in St. Leo and an original "Cracker House'' in Holiday. Camp at Starkey Wilderness Park, cast your fishing line at Anclote River Park, paddle a kayak at Werner Boyce Salt Spring State Park. Hike the Suncoast Trail, visit spots along the Great Florida Birding Trail or charter a deep sea fishing excursion.


From the beaches on the Gulf Coast to scenic rivers like the Withlacoochee in the east to one of the world's premier drop zones at Skydive City, Pasco has something for everyone. See local and national acts perform at the Show Palace in Hudson and historic Richey Suncoast Theater in New Port Richey. Savor locally-made wines at the Florida Estates Winery in Land O' Lakes. Enjoy dozens of unique festivals, including Chasco Fiesta in New Port Richey and the Kumquat Festival in Dade City.

title: Morningside Nature Center "Go Native" Plant Sale
venue: Department of Parks, Recreation and Cultural Affairs
description:
Experience culture in Gainesville, Florida.

The Gainesville area is home to not only the Florida Gators but many cultural and eco-heritage sites including the Harn Museum of Art, the Thomas Center and  Gallery, Phillips Center for the Performing Arts, Florida Museum of Natural History, Hippodrome State Theater, University Auditorium, Santa Fe Community College Zoo, Morningside Nature Center and Paynes Prairie. Experience an exciting journey in Gainesville, Florida.

title: Jazz & Blues Festival
description: The Tallahassee Museum is located on 52 acres of scenic woodlands in Southwest Tallahassee bordering beautiful Lake Bradford. The city's oldest museum chronicles the history and heritage of north Florida and south Georgia. A key feature is the 1880s farmstead with live farm animals, a legacy garden and living-history demonstrations from spinning to cane-grinding. Historic structures also include Bellevue plantation house and quarters, Concord one-room schoolhouse, 1920s Seaboard Air Line Caboose (climb aboard!), Bethlehem Missionary Baptist Church, a gristmill and an historic commissary. Its natural habitat zoo features Florida panthers, red wolves, black bears, river otters, birds of prey and other native and rare wildlife. Up close Animal Encounters with wildlife are offered daily. Exotic animals are exhibited seasonally. The Phipps Gallery presents exhibits of artistic and scholarly interest pertaining to regional history and heritage. The Education staff presents a vast array of public workshops and activities throughout the year. The Museum also offers a hands-on Discovery Center, Trail Break Cafe, Gift Shop and playground. Plus, on-site pre-school, voluntary pre-K, and summer camps. Inspiring, educational fun for all ages, with attention to accessibility. See video clips and learn more at their website.

title: Panhandle Pioneer Settlement FOLK LIFE DAYS
description: Explore Florida's past through living history, hands-on exhibits, re-created period buildings and archaeological excavations at the only reconstructed Spanish mission in Florida. Guided group tours available by reservation. The council house is the largest historic Indian building in the Southeast. The site was the capital of Florida's western missions from 1656 to 1704. It was home to 1,500 Spanish and Apalachee Indian residents. San Luis is a "Preserve America" Presidential Award Recipient.

title: Natural Science Lecture Series: \"Climate Change, Sea Level Rise, and its Effect on SWFL Gulf Coast\"
description:
Sanibel & Captiva are considered the shelling capital of North America. More than 300 species of shells can be found in the shallow water surrounding the islands.

The Bailey-Matthews Shell Museum is the only museum in the country dedicated entirely to shells. Over thirty exhibits tell the story of mollusks from around the world. Exhibits are devoted to shells in art and history, shell habitats, rare specimens, fossil shells and common Southwest Florida shells. Two live mollusk videos alternate continuously every 30 minutes.

Children are mesmerized by the children’s learning lab featuring a hands-on play area and a “live tank” with indigenous mollusks. This area provides a golden opportunity for children to experience the museum rather than merely observing exhibits. A half-hour video, Mollusks in Action, is shown on the hour and a children's video is shown continuously.

The museum is passionate about children’s education. The goal is for the museum to come alive as an exciting learning center instead of just a building.

Young girls are in awe when they discover that at one time shells were used as money and a bride’s value was calculated “in shells.” Many children stare in disbelief when learning that shells are actually made by a creature and the creature has a self propelling foot, a mouth and in the case of scallops, even eyes.

Summer Camps, Mommy and Me Play Sessions, a Youth Docent Program, half-day workshops, and a puppet theater are designed to help children discover the wonder of the world of shells. Children can even “shell-a-brate” their birthdays at the museum.

An exquisite gift shop offers a wide variety of unique shell-themed gifts including books, ceramics, clothing, toys and fine jewelry.

Open daily from 10 a.m. - 5 p.m. Thanksgiving, Christmas, New Year’s, Easter and the first Sunday in March are the only days the museum is closed. Admission is $7.00 for adults seventeen and up, $4.00 for youth five - 16 years of age and children four and under are free. Located close to “Ding” Darling National Wildlife Refuge. Call for program information or to register for classes. Visit their website for more information and a complete listing of programs and events.

title: Party for the Planet
venue: Central Florida Zoo and Botanical Gardens
description:
Enter the enchanted, tropical world of the Central Florida Zoo & Botanical Gardens, a relaxing, entertaining and educational experience for the entire family. You’ll discover a world of animals from around the world within this tropical park nestled in the heart of Florida. Stroll along shaded, winding boardwalks and paths as you see towering elephants, search for the elusive cheetah, appreciate the beauty of the hyacinth macaw and listen to the song of the kookaburra. Hop on over to the Horizon Homes of Central Florida Australia exhibit featuring emus and kangaroos or dare to meet some of the world’s most venomous reptiles and non-venomous snakes, lizards and frogs in the Herpetarium. Feed goats, sheep, llamas, zebus, and other domestic animals in the Animal Adventure area. Don’t miss the native wildlife that resides in the lush, tropical setting of the Zoo.

There's always something new to see at the Zoo including the recently opened Wharton-Smith Tropical Splash Ground! So bring your swimsuit and flip-flops and jump in to cool off.  Afterwards, take a peek at the endangered Amur leopards, the venomous king cobra, the slow sloth and watch the siamangs, king vultures and cougar enjoy habitats to swing, fly and relax. The Butterfly Sensory Garden incorporates touch, look, listen and smell stations to show how insect senses differ from those of humans in addition to the many plant varieties featured to attract and support all stages of the butterfly or take a ride on Champ the Train or a spin on the Animal Carousel.

Among the most popular programs is the up-close and personal Animal Encounters on weekends and holidays, in which docents educate visitors about the characteristics of animals from alligators to hedgehogs to snakes. Other popular weekend programs include an elephant demonstration, bird training, and feeding programs for felines and primates. Behind-the-Scenes Elephant Encounters offer visitors a once-in-a-lifetime experience to feed and touch the Asian elephants.

With something for everyone, the adventures are endless!

description: A premier skydiving resort for first-timers, vacationers, spectators and experienced skydivers alike. title: Easter Sunrise Service
description: Jewel of the Suwannee Set amid the lush greenery, winding waterways and native wilderness, North Florida is one of the Sunshine State's little known and most precious treasures.  Cut from nature's flawless beauty and set apart by a band of shimmering waters, this sparkling gem reflects the many colorful facets of Florida's rich history and original unspoiled splendor.  It is here in crystal-clear waters, under sapphire skies and golden sun, shaded by an emerald canopy of green that visitors discover Hamilton County, Florida - the "Jewel of the Suwannee".Resting on the Florida-Georgia border, Hamilton County is truely set apart from the rest of the state.  Bordered by the Withlacoochee River to the west and the World Famous Suwannee River to the east and south, the county forms a penisula within a penisula, uniquely separated from the landmass of Florida.  Neatly splitting this river county is the twisting Alapaha River, adding to the vitality and beauty of a paradise for nature lovers and outdoor sports enthusiasts for all ages.  The protected waters of Hamilton County's rivers, crystal clear springs and numberous lakes provide endless opportunities for outdoor activities.  Whether camping, hunting, photography or just exploring by foot, bike, horseback, canoe or kayak, you'll find it to be the "Jewel of the Suwannee".  A Tale of Two Treasures  While Hamilton County is undeniably a natural treasure, it is equally valuable as one of Florida's historic treasures.  With more than 150 sites and structures on the National Register of Historic Places, Hamilton County is a popular destination for both casual history buffs and the more serious genealogy researchers, the county is landscaped with more than 50 county cemeteries, including what is believed to be Florida's oldest.  For those who will listen, these weathered tombstones and grave markers just may whisper a tale.Hamilton County, better known as the "Jewel of the Suwannee" says, "come for a visit, stay for a lifetime".  While visiting Hamilton Couty , we invite you to visit the 888-acre Stephen Foster Folk Culture Center State Park in quaint White Springs - home to the first hub of the Suwannee River Wilderness Trail and Florida Trail.

title: Reflections: Paintings of Florida 1865-1965
description:
HistoryMiami is the premier cultural institution committed to gathering, organizing, preserving and celebrating Miami’s history as the unique crossroads of the Americas. Through exhibitions, city tours, education, research, collections and publications, HistoryMiami advocates for helping everyone understand the importance of the past in shaping Miami‘s future.

Formerly known as the Historical Museum of Southern Florida, HistoryMiami was founded in 1940 as a historical association comprised of famous Miamians including George Merrick, Charlton Tebeau and Marjory Stoneman Douglas. The Association established the first museum for regular public use in 1962 and ten years later, moved to a larger facility adjacent to the Miami Science Museum and Vizcaya Museum and Gardens, expanding its exhibition and educational programs. From 1974 to 1979, the Historical Museum of Southern Florida focused on developing storyline exhibitions and its professional staff. In 1984, the Historical Museum moved to downtown Miami, the site of its present facility in the Miami-Dade Cultural Center.

On April 29, 2010, the Historical Museum of Southern Florida was officially renamed to HistoryMiami. The Museum is one of the largest private, regional history museums in the state. It offers exhibitions that appeal to a wide audience interested in the South Florida and the Caribbean community, while at the same time engaging to residents and tourists alike.

Home to more than 35,000 three-dimensional artifacts, including a 1920s trolley car; Seminole and Miccosukee Indian objects; artifacts from Pan American Airways and Eastern Airlines; musical instruments and religious items from local communities; and outboard motors. 

The HistoryMiami Archives and Research Center collects, safeguards, and makes accessible materials that document the Miami region, South Florida and the Caribbean. The collection includes a rare, complete double elephant folio edition of John James Audubon’s The Birds of America, as well as 6,000 bound volumes, 1,900 maps and more than one million historic photographs.

You can also delve into the past and experience the sights, sounds and culture of South Florida with the nationally acclaimed City Tours program. Whether by boat, coach, walking or biking, City Tours offer the opportunity to discover the hidden secrets and neighborhoods you never knew existed.

description:
Immerse yourself in 4,000 years of diving history!   From the ancient days of Gilgamesh to the modern days of recreational diving, divers and non-divers alike will enjoy this interactive museum telling the story of mankind’s quest to explore under the sea.
• What did Astronomer Edmund Halley contribute to the evolution of modern day diving equipment? Come sit in a replica of his invention.
• What did a resourceful bystander to an 1827 fire in a horse barn contribute? Marvel at the ingenuity and bravery of inventors over the ages.
• Try out your muscles in our pump room and be thankful for advancements in technology to SCUBA!
• Military and commercial divers enjoy reminiscing about using the old-time gear and seeing how things have changed since their diving days…and how some things a have stayed the same.

The History of Diving Museum features the world’s largest international collection of diving helmets and artifacts. Visitors from around the world are warmly welcomed, with exhibit guides available in 8 languages, English, Spanish, German, Portuguese, Dutch, French, Russian and Italian.

Shoppers will appreciate the rare and unique treasures available in the Museum Store. The store features quality undersea themed items perfect for gifts or to complement your diving lifestyle. Choose from fine historical prints suitable for framing, maps of shipwreck sites, a comprehensive selection of diving and related books, as well as jewelry, apparel and a special children’s area.

Visitors to the History of Diving Museum comment:
“The best collection of deep sea diving equipment I have ever seen.” “What a great collection. We enjoyed the visit tremendously.” “Amazing. Informative, insightful – a valuable experience.” “Great museum for the young and older generation!” “Totally unexpected fun & informative.”

title: Wild Animals Hunt for Easter Eggs at Naples Zoo
description:
Much more than a walk-thru zoo, this historic tropical garden with mature botanicals and nationally accredited zoo features a full day of wildlife experiences to delight guests with the natural world to inspire the conservation of our planet's remaining wild areas and their wondrous inhabitants. 


Daily presentations include the hand-feeding of giant reptiles at Alligator Bay, Meet the Keeper Series, Jungle Larry & Safari Jane's Snakes Alive, along with two premiere presentations in the Safari Canyon theater where guests see live animals from feline predators to venomous snakes along with exciting video footage. A guided tour of the historic garden is offered on Sundays. One of the zoo’s most popular activities is the Primate Expedition Cruise where guests embark on a guided cruise past islands inhabited by monkeys, lemurs, and apes. Guests enjoy seeing favorites like lions, monkeys, zebras, and the new Giraffe Preview Exhibit. They also discover rarely seen species like Malagasy fosas and Parma wallabies. At large glass walls, they get wildly close to carnivores at exhibits like Leopard Rock, Tiger Forest, Black Bear Hammock, and Panther Glade.


Along with all that’s new, Naples Zoo has a wonderful history beginning in 1919 when botanist Dr. Henry Nehrling founded the garden. After his death, the trees grew wild until a Fleischmann Yeast heir expanded the forgotten garden in 1954. In 1969, Lawrence and Nancy Jane Tetzlaff, a.k.a. Jungle Larry and Safari Jane, introduced the wild animals. Larry did stunt work for Johnny Weissmuller in the famous Tarzan films, milked thousands of venomous snakes during WWII, and educated millions of adults and children throughout the Midwest and Florida with his wife Nancy. Since that time, the Zoo earned national accreditation and won both regional and national awards. 


Today, the 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization cooperates in conservation programs both in and outside the wild for endangered species. Naples Zoo was one of the first in the nation to include a 25 cent fee with each admission to fund conservation programs in the wild. Naples Zoo also plants a tree in Africa, Asia, or the Americas for each child visiting on a school field trip or guest attending a corporate event -- and even more trees for guests who become Zoo Members. 10% of the price of each stuffed plush predator or primate also funds conservation programs. Your visit makes a better world.

title: BREAKFAST IN THE PARK
description:
A Place for Retreat and Renewal on Florida's Nature Coast

Experience 636 acres of natural Florida at Otter Springs Park & Campground.

Our centerpiece, Otter Springs, is a second magnitude natural spring with a constant temperature of 73 degrees and a flow of 10 million gallons of sparkling pure water daily. The spring creates a large clear pool and stream, which flows into the nearby Suwannee River.

The serene setting is perfect for fishing, bird watching, hiking, biking and other outdoor activities.  We have miles of trails in the park and are close to the Nature Coast State Trail.  Indoors at the Little Otter Club we offer a gym, board games, foosball, and cards.  We also have ladder golf, washer toss, croquet and horseshoes.

And when you want a little bit of both indoor comfort and outdoor beauty, relax at a poolside table or swim laps in our spacious, enclosed pool pavilion.

title: Easter Boogie
description:
At the northern end of the Tampa Bay area, beautiful Pasco County is close to major cities but far from the hustle and bustle. Visit Pasco and enjoy Florida the way it used to be. Acres of pristine wilderness with biking, hiking and canoeing trails. Historic downtowns with fine restaurants and antique shops and dozens of family-oriented activities and sporting events year 'round. Pasco County is home to world-class tennis and golf resorts, including Saddlebrook Resort & Spa, one of Conde Nast Traveler's Top 100 and Lake Jovita, the Florida course that plays like North Carolina. 


Enjoy cultural treasures, such as the Historic Courthouse, built in 1909 in beautiful downtown Dade City and the Pioneer Florida Museum, home to period buildings dating to 1878. Experience historic walking tours of downtown New Port Richey, boat tours of the Pithlachascotee River and trolley tours in downtown Dade City. See the World War II Barracks Museum in Zephyrhills, the St. Leo Abbey & Grotto in St. Leo and an original "Cracker House'' in Holiday. Camp at Starkey Wilderness Park, cast your fishing line at Anclote River Park, paddle a kayak at Werner Boyce Salt Spring State Park. Hike the Suncoast Trail, visit spots along the Great Florida Birding Trail or charter a deep sea fishing excursion.


From the beaches on the Gulf Coast to scenic rivers like the Withlacoochee in the east to one of the world's premier drop zones at Skydive City, Pasco has something for everyone. See local and national acts perform at the Show Palace in Hudson and historic Richey Suncoast Theater in New Port Richey. Savor locally-made wines at the Florida Estates Winery in Land O' Lakes. Enjoy dozens of unique festivals, including Chasco Fiesta in New Port Richey and the Kumquat Festival in Dade City.

title: 47th Annual Easter Surfing Festival
venue: Florida\'s Space Coast Office of Tourism
description: Visit Florida's Space Coast, Orlando's closest beaches (just one hour east) and home to NASA's Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex, US Astronaut Hall of Fame and Port Canaveral Cruises to the Bahamas and Caribbean.  Offering plenty of eco-tourism opportunities at Merritt Island National Wildlife Refuge, Brevard Zoo, Canaveral National Seashore and the Indian River Lagoon.  There's great fishing on the freshwater St. Johns River and on the saltwater Indian River Lagoon as well as deep-see angling in the Atlantic Ocean.  Over 25 golf courses will challenge the beginner or pro.  Be sure to check our website for Special Offers and an easy way to reserve your hotel room!  Email or call for the Space Coast Vacation Planner listing all our accommodations and attractions.

title: Ron Jon Easter Surfing Festival
description: Located on 700 feet of pristine beach, one mile from Port Canaveral and it's cruise ships. Close to Kennedy Space Center and only 45 miles from Orlando! Complimentary daily continental breakfast and wine and cheese social Friday evenings, including beer and appetizers. Daily housekeeping service available. Free Wi-Fi access. Free cable with HBO. title: Beach Blast Triathlon/Duathlon

description: A quiet coastal community where preserved natural beauty makes for a spellbinding vacation. Shelling, watching dolphins play and dipping into the Gulf waters are favorite pastimes. They invite you to share in an experience that's perhaps the Florida Panhandle's best-kept secret. They just ask one thing, don't tell too many people about them.

On-site amenities include five restaurants, 45-holes of golf, 18 Har-Tru tennis courts, Island House Spa with massage therapy and body treatments, fitness center, year-round Kids Klub, full-service deep water marina and miles of white sand beach. Eight miles from Sarasota/Bradenton Airport and 65 from Tampa Airport. Meeting facilities for groups ups to 160 and ideal location for destination weddings.

title: Red, White, and ZOO
venue: Central Florida Zoo and Botanical Gardens
description:
Enter the enchanted, tropical world of the Central Florida Zoo & Botanical Gardens, a relaxing, entertaining and educational experience for the entire family. You’ll discover a world of animals from around the world within this tropical park nestled in the heart of Florida. Stroll along shaded, winding boardwalks and paths as you see towering elephants, search for the elusive cheetah, appreciate the beauty of the hyacinth macaw and listen to the song of the kookaburra. Hop on over to the Horizon Homes of Central Florida Australia exhibit featuring emus and kangaroos or dare to meet some of the world’s most venomous reptiles and non-venomous snakes, lizards and frogs in the Herpetarium. Feed goats, sheep, llamas, zebus, and other domestic animals in the Animal Adventure area. Don’t miss the native wildlife that resides in the lush, tropical setting of the Zoo.

There's always something new to see at the Zoo including the recently opened Wharton-Smith Tropical Splash Ground! So bring your swimsuit and flip-flops and jump in to cool off.  Afterwards, take a peek at the endangered Amur leopards, the venomous king cobra, the slow sloth and watch the siamangs, king vultures and cougar enjoy habitats to swing, fly and relax. The Butterfly Sensory Garden incorporates touch, look, listen and smell stations to show how insect senses differ from those of humans in addition to the many plant varieties featured to attract and support all stages of the butterfly or take a ride on Champ the Train or a spin on the Animal Carousel.

Among the most popular programs is the up-close and personal Animal Encounters on weekends and holidays, in which docents educate visitors about the characteristics of animals from alligators to hedgehogs to snakes. Other popular weekend programs include an elephant demonstration, bird training, and feeding programs for felines and primates. Behind-the-Scenes Elephant Encounters offer visitors a once-in-a-lifetime experience to feed and touch the Asian elephants.

With something for everyone, the adventures are endless!

title: Prime Rib Night
description:
A hidden gem located in the "Nature Coast" of Florida on the Gulf of Mexico, our beautiful eco-friendly and  green lodging resort is surrounded by the natural springs of King's Bay in Crystal River and home to over 400 West Indian Manatee who migrate each winter to the constant 72 degree springs and to the only place in the Country where you can legally swim with these gentle giants.


The resort rests on 232 acres of lush greens, emerald pines and grand oaks is manicured with great precision.  Our196 well appointed and spacious guest rooms and suites which include 12 two story golf villas with a spectacular view of the golf course offer the comfort of true hospitality and a tranquil experience.


Our Marina and Dive Shop offers great water activities, boat rentals, kayak rentals, canoe rentals, guided river tours, scuba diving tours, PADI certification and Manatee snorkel tours during the peak season from October to March,  we do have year round Manatee residence but recommend tours during peak winter months.  


The finest of Florida golf rave our golf enthusiasts who travel to conquer our Mark Mahannah designed 18 holes championship course; you can mix and match our three nines to suit your particular strength or weakness.  If it’s a short course you prefer, our 9 hole Lagoons course and is a great option to sharpen your short game.  Our links are beautifully manicured and well groomed; the course has a variety of water and bunker obstacles.  The course has aged well and offers an assortment of challenging fairways lined with mature emerald pines, grand oaks and is home to much wildlife.


Our full service Aveda Spa offers; hair, nail and skincare services as well as couples massage room with a working fireplace and a perfect setting for a romantic getaway or that honeymoon that you never took.


We have a lagoon style heated swimming pool and a Jacuzzi overlooking the beautiful river; we offer our guests food and beverage service from our Tiki bar which is open seasonally. 


The Plantation Room is our main dining room and offers breakfast, lunch and dinner service, we also have a Library bar a great central gathering place, our Tiki bar is open seasonally and is well attended by guests and neighbors who can pull up their boat and enjoy our great culinary fare and the beautiful Florida sunshine.  Our Pro-Bar offers a great menu for those golfers who want a quick burger or our wonderful members who enjoy a great sandwich, cold beverage a perfect view of the golf course.

title: Prime Rib Night
description:
A hidden gem located in the "Nature Coast" of Florida on the Gulf of Mexico, our beautiful eco-friendly and  green lodging resort is surrounded by the natural springs of King's Bay in Crystal River and home to over 400 West Indian Manatee who migrate each winter to the constant 72 degree springs and to the only place in the Country where you can legally swim with these gentle giants.


The resort rests on 232 acres of lush greens, emerald pines and grand oaks is manicured with great precision.  Our196 well appointed and spacious guest rooms and suites which include 12 two story golf villas with a spectacular view of the golf course offer the comfort of true hospitality and a tranquil experience.


Our Marina and Dive Shop offers great water activities, boat rentals, kayak rentals, canoe rentals, guided river tours, scuba diving tours, PADI certification and Manatee snorkel tours during the peak season from October to March,  we do have year round Manatee residence but recommend tours during peak winter months.  


The finest of Florida golf rave our golf enthusiasts who travel to conquer our Mark Mahannah designed 18 holes championship course; you can mix and match our three nines to suit your particular strength or weakness.  If it’s a short course you prefer, our 9 hole Lagoons course and is a great option to sharpen your short game.  Our links are beautifully manicured and well groomed; the course has a variety of water and bunker obstacles.  The course has aged well and offers an assortment of challenging fairways lined with mature emerald pines, grand oaks and is home to much wildlife.


Our full service Aveda Spa offers; hair, nail and skincare services as well as couples massage room with a working fireplace and a perfect setting for a romantic getaway or that honeymoon that you never took.


We have a lagoon style heated swimming pool and a Jacuzzi overlooking the beautiful river; we offer our guests food and beverage service from our Tiki bar which is open seasonally. 


The Plantation Room is our main dining room and offers breakfast, lunch and dinner service, we also have a Library bar a great central gathering place, our Tiki bar is open seasonally and is well attended by guests and neighbors who can pull up their boat and enjoy our great culinary fare and the beautiful Florida sunshine.  Our Pro-Bar offers a great menu for those golfers who want a quick burger or our wonderful members who enjoy a great sandwich, cold beverage a perfect view of the golf course.

title: Open Receptions for \"3D Art - No Glasses Needed\"
description:
At the northern end of the Tampa Bay area, beautiful Pasco County is close to major cities but far from the hustle and bustle. Visit Pasco and enjoy Florida the way it used to be. Acres of pristine wilderness with biking, hiking and canoeing trails. Historic downtowns with fine restaurants and antique shops and dozens of family-oriented activities and sporting events year 'round. Pasco County is home to world-class tennis and golf resorts, including Saddlebrook Resort & Spa, one of Conde Nast Traveler's Top 100 and Lake Jovita, the Florida course that plays like North Carolina. 


Enjoy cultural treasures, such as the Historic Courthouse, built in 1909 in beautiful downtown Dade City and the Pioneer Florida Museum, home to period buildings dating to 1878. Experience historic walking tours of downtown New Port Richey, boat tours of the Pithlachascotee River and trolley tours in downtown Dade City. See the World War II Barracks Museum in Zephyrhills, the St. Leo Abbey & Grotto in St. Leo and an original "Cracker House'' in Holiday. Camp at Starkey Wilderness Park, cast your fishing line at Anclote River Park, paddle a kayak at Werner Boyce Salt Spring State Park. Hike the Suncoast Trail, visit spots along the Great Florida Birding Trail or charter a deep sea fishing excursion.


From the beaches on the Gulf Coast to scenic rivers like the Withlacoochee in the east to one of the world's premier drop zones at Skydive City, Pasco has something for everyone. See local and national acts perform at the Show Palace in Hudson and historic Richey Suncoast Theater in New Port Richey. Savor locally-made wines at the Florida Estates Winery in Land O' Lakes. Enjoy dozens of unique festivals, including Chasco Fiesta in New Port Richey and the Kumquat Festival in Dade City.

A hidden gem located in the "Nature Coast" of Florida on the Gulf of Mexico, our beautiful eco-friendly and  green lodging resort is surrounded by the natural springs of King's Bay in Crystal River and home to over 400 West Indian Manatee who migrate each winter to the constant 72 degree springs and to the only place in the Country where you can legally swim with these gentle giants.


The resort rests on 232 acres of lush greens, emerald pines and grand oaks is manicured with great precision.  Our196 well appointed and spacious guest rooms and suites which include 12 two story golf villas with a spectacular view of the golf course offer the comfort of true hospitality and a tranquil experience.


Our Marina and Dive Shop offers great water activities, boat rentals, kayak rentals, canoe rentals, guided river tours, scuba diving tours, PADI certification and Manatee snorkel tours during the peak season from October to March,  we do have year round Manatee residence but recommend tours during peak winter months.  


The finest of Florida golf rave our golf enthusiasts who travel to conquer our Mark Mahannah designed 18 holes championship course; you can mix and match our three nines to suit your particular strength or weakness.  If it’s a short course you prefer, our 9 hole Lagoons course and is a great option to sharpen your short game.  Our links are beautifully manicured and well groomed; the course has a variety of water and bunker obstacles.  The course has aged well and offers an assortment of challenging fairways lined with mature emerald pines, grand oaks and is home to much wildlife.


Our full service Aveda Spa offers; hair, nail and skincare services as well as couples massage room with a working fireplace and a perfect setting for a romantic getaway or that honeymoon that you never took.


We have a lagoon style heated swimming pool and a Jacuzzi overlooking the beautiful river; we offer our guests food and beverage service from our Tiki bar which is open seasonally. 


The Plantation Room is our main dining room and offers breakfast, lunch and dinner service, we also have a Library bar a great central gathering place, our Tiki bar is open seasonally and is well attended by guests and neighbors who can pull up their boat and enjoy our great culinary fare and the beautiful Florida sunshine.  Our Pro-Bar offers a great menu for those golfers who want a quick burger or our wonderful members who enjoy a great sandwich, cold beverage a perfect view of the golf course.

title: 4th Fridays in Artisan Alley & DeLand Art Walk
description:
Downtown DeLand is an award winning MainStreet community where we have learned to cherish that which is special about our past while still planning and moving into the 21st Century. MainStreet DeLand has many dedicated merchants and volunteers who work daily to maintain a lively and economically successful downtown.

We invite you to see for yourself what makes MainStreet DeLand so special. Spend a day downtown browsing our shops and galleries; dine at one of our great restaurants; have a coffee pick-me-up in one of our specialty coffee shops. You won't be disappointed!

title: \"Recent Acquisitions\" exhibition.
description: Appleton Museum offers exciting temporary art exhibitions as well as world class permanent collections of European, American, Contemporary art, plus African, Asian, Islamic and pre-Columbian artifacts and antiquities. Other programs include educational art films, painting workshops, lectures, musical programs, special events and guided excursions to other art museums and historic destinations.

title: Bonnet House Fine Artists Exhibitions
description: An extraordinary blend of art, architecture, history and ecology. This 35-acre subtropical estate and historic house museum was designed by Frederic Clay Bartlett, a noted painter and art collector. Bonnet House is one of the few complete homes and studios of two American artists with original furnishings open to the public. A nature trail walk taking up to 30 minutes is available. Guided golf cart tour of nature trail available. Outdoor rental space available.

title: A Summer Place
description: The historic Martin County Court House Cultural Center hosts fine arts exhibits featuring locally and nationally known artists. Home to the Arts Council, it serves as an arts and cultural information center. This 1937 WPA project is a rare example of post-depression Art Deco. The Arts Council also coordinates many events each year, including ArtsFest - a two day, fine arts, crafts and music festival and publishes MartinArts magazine with an event calendar and resources listings.

title: Prime Rib Night
description:
A hidden gem located in the "Nature Coast" of Florida on the Gulf of Mexico, our beautiful eco-friendly and  green lodging resort is surrounded by the natural springs of King's Bay in Crystal River and home to over 400 West Indian Manatee who migrate each winter to the constant 72 degree springs and to the only place in the Country where you can legally swim with these gentle giants.


The resort rests on 232 acres of lush greens, emerald pines and grand oaks is manicured with great precision.  Our196 well appointed and spacious guest rooms and suites which include 12 two story golf villas with a spectacular view of the golf course offer the comfort of true hospitality and a tranquil experience.


Our Marina and Dive Shop offers great water activities, boat rentals, kayak rentals, canoe rentals, guided river tours, scuba diving tours, PADI certification and Manatee snorkel tours during the peak season from October to March,  we do have year round Manatee residence but recommend tours during peak winter months.  


The finest of Florida golf rave our golf enthusiasts who travel to conquer our Mark Mahannah designed 18 holes championship course; you can mix and match our three nines to suit your particular strength or weakness.  If it’s a short course you prefer, our 9 hole Lagoons course and is a great option to sharpen your short game.  Our links are beautifully manicured and well groomed; the course has a variety of water and bunker obstacles.  The course has aged well and offers an assortment of challenging fairways lined with mature emerald pines, grand oaks and is home to much wildlife.


Our full service Aveda Spa offers; hair, nail and skincare services as well as couples massage room with a working fireplace and a perfect setting for a romantic getaway or that honeymoon that you never took.


We have a lagoon style heated swimming pool and a Jacuzzi overlooking the beautiful river; we offer our guests food and beverage service from our Tiki bar which is open seasonally. 


The Plantation Room is our main dining room and offers breakfast, lunch and dinner service, we also have a Library bar a great central gathering place, our Tiki bar is open seasonally and is well attended by guests and neighbors who can pull up their boat and enjoy our great culinary fare and the beautiful Florida sunshine.  Our Pro-Bar offers a great menu for those golfers who want a quick burger or our wonderful members who enjoy a great sandwich, cold beverage a perfect view of the golf course.

title: Creative Arts in the Park Day
description: Jewel of the Suwannee Set amid the lush greenery, winding waterways and native wilderness, North Florida is one of the Sunshine State's little known and most precious treasures.  Cut from nature's flawless beauty and set apart by a band of shimmering waters, this sparkling gem reflects the many colorful facets of Florida's rich history and original unspoiled splendor.  It is here in crystal-clear waters, under sapphire skies and golden sun, shaded by an emerald canopy of green that visitors discover Hamilton County, Florida - the "Jewel of the Suwannee".Resting on the Florida-Georgia border, Hamilton County is truely set apart from the rest of the state.  Bordered by the Withlacoochee River to the west and the World Famous Suwannee River to the east and south, the county forms a penisula within a penisula, uniquely separated from the landmass of Florida.  Neatly splitting this river county is the twisting Alapaha River, adding to the vitality and beauty of a paradise for nature lovers and outdoor sports enthusiasts for all ages.  The protected waters of Hamilton County's rivers, crystal clear springs and numberous lakes provide endless opportunities for outdoor activities.  Whether camping, hunting, photography or just exploring by foot, bike, horseback, canoe or kayak, you'll find it to be the "Jewel of the Suwannee".  A Tale of Two Treasures  While Hamilton County is undeniably a natural treasure, it is equally valuable as one of Florida's historic treasures.  With more than 150 sites and structures on the National Register of Historic Places, Hamilton County is a popular destination for both casual history buffs and the more serious genealogy researchers, the county is landscaped with more than 50 county cemeteries, including what is believed to be Florida's oldest.  For those who will listen, these weathered tombstones and grave markers just may whisper a tale.Hamilton County, better known as the "Jewel of the Suwannee" says, "come for a visit, stay for a lifetime".  While visiting Hamilton Couty , we invite you to visit the 888-acre Stephen Foster Folk Culture Center State Park in quaint White Springs - home to the first hub of the Suwannee River Wilderness Trail and Florida Trail.

title: Prime Rib Night
description:
A hidden gem located in the "Nature Coast" of Florida on the Gulf of Mexico, our beautiful eco-friendly and  green lodging resort is surrounded by the natural springs of King's Bay in Crystal River and home to over 400 West Indian Manatee who migrate each winter to the constant 72 degree springs and to the only place in the Country where you can legally swim with these gentle giants.


The resort rests on 232 acres of lush greens, emerald pines and grand oaks is manicured with great precision.  Our196 well appointed and spacious guest rooms and suites which include 12 two story golf villas with a spectacular view of the golf course offer the comfort of true hospitality and a tranquil experience.


Our Marina and Dive Shop offers great water activities, boat rentals, kayak rentals, canoe rentals, guided river tours, scuba diving tours, PADI certification and Manatee snorkel tours during the peak season from October to March,  we do have year round Manatee residence but recommend tours during peak winter months.  


The finest of Florida golf rave our golf enthusiasts who travel to conquer our Mark Mahannah designed 18 holes championship course; you can mix and match our three nines to suit your particular strength or weakness.  If it’s a short course you prefer, our 9 hole Lagoons course and is a great option to sharpen your short game.  Our links are beautifully manicured and well groomed; the course has a variety of water and bunker obstacles.  The course has aged well and offers an assortment of challenging fairways lined with mature emerald pines, grand oaks and is home to much wildlife.


Our full service Aveda Spa offers; hair, nail and skincare services as well as couples massage room with a working fireplace and a perfect setting for a romantic getaway or that honeymoon that you never took.


We have a lagoon style heated swimming pool and a Jacuzzi overlooking the beautiful river; we offer our guests food and beverage service from our Tiki bar which is open seasonally. 


The Plantation Room is our main dining room and offers breakfast, lunch and dinner service, we also have a Library bar a great central gathering place, our Tiki bar is open seasonally and is well attended by guests and neighbors who can pull up their boat and enjoy our great culinary fare and the beautiful Florida sunshine.  Our Pro-Bar offers a great menu for those golfers who want a quick burger or our wonderful members who enjoy a great sandwich, cold beverage a perfect view of the golf course.

description: An extraordinary blend of art, architecture, history and ecology. This 35-acre subtropical estate and historic house museum was designed by Frederic Clay Bartlett, a noted painter and art collector. Bonnet House is one of the few complete homes and studios of two American artists with original furnishings open to the public. A nature trail walk taking up to 30 minutes is available. Guided golf cart tour of nature trail available. Outdoor rental space available.

The resort rests on 232 acres of lush greens, emerald pines and grand oaks is manicured with great precision.  Our196 well appointed and spacious guest rooms and suites which include 12 two story golf villas with a spectacular view of the golf course offer the comfort of true hospitality and a tranquil experience.


Our Marina and Dive Shop offers great water activities, boat rentals, kayak rentals, canoe rentals, guided river tours, scuba diving tours, PADI certification and Manatee snorkel tours during the peak season from October to March,  we do have year round Manatee residence but recommend tours during peak winter months.  


The finest of Florida golf rave our golf enthusiasts who travel to conquer our Mark Mahannah designed 18 holes championship course; you can mix and match our three nines to suit your particular strength or weakness.  If it’s a short course you prefer, our 9 hole Lagoons course and is a great option to sharpen your short game.  Our links are beautifully manicured and well groomed; the course has a variety of water and bunker obstacles.  The course has aged well and offers an assortment of challenging fairways lined with mature emerald pines, grand oaks and is home to much wildlife.


Our full service Aveda Spa offers; hair, nail and skincare services as well as couples massage room with a working fireplace and a perfect setting for a romantic getaway or that honeymoon that you never took.


We have a lagoon style heated swimming pool and a Jacuzzi overlooking the beautiful river; we offer our guests food and beverage service from our Tiki bar which is open seasonally. 


The Plantation Room is our main dining room and offers breakfast, lunch and dinner service, we also have a Library bar a great central gathering place, our Tiki bar is open seasonally and is well attended by guests and neighbors who can pull up their boat and enjoy our great culinary fare and the beautiful Florida sunshine.  Our Pro-Bar offers a great menu for those golfers who want a quick burger or our wonderful members who enjoy a great sandwich, cold beverage a perfect view of the golf course.

title: Bonnet House Fine Artists Exhibitions
description: An extraordinary blend of art, architecture, history and ecology. This 35-acre subtropical estate and historic house museum was designed by Frederic Clay Bartlett, a noted painter and art collector. Bonnet House is one of the few complete homes and studios of two American artists with original furnishings open to the public. A nature trail walk taking up to 30 minutes is available. Guided golf cart tour of nature trail available. Outdoor rental space available.

The resort rests on 232 acres of lush greens, emerald pines and grand oaks is manicured with great precision.  Our196 well appointed and spacious guest rooms and suites which include 12 two story golf villas with a spectacular view of the golf course offer the comfort of true hospitality and a tranquil experience.


Our Marina and Dive Shop offers great water activities, boat rentals, kayak rentals, canoe rentals, guided river tours, scuba diving tours, PADI certification and Manatee snorkel tours during the peak season from October to March,  we do have year round Manatee residence but recommend tours during peak winter months.  


The finest of Florida golf rave our golf enthusiasts who travel to conquer our Mark Mahannah designed 18 holes championship course; you can mix and match our three nines to suit your particular strength or weakness.  If it’s a short course you prefer, our 9 hole Lagoons course and is a great option to sharpen your short game.  Our links are beautifully manicured and well groomed; the course has a variety of water and bunker obstacles.  The course has aged well and offers an assortment of challenging fairways lined with mature emerald pines, grand oaks and is home to much wildlife.


Our full service Aveda Spa offers; hair, nail and skincare services as well as couples massage room with a working fireplace and a perfect setting for a romantic getaway or that honeymoon that you never took.


We have a lagoon style heated swimming pool and a Jacuzzi overlooking the beautiful river; we offer our guests food and beverage service from our Tiki bar which is open seasonally. 


The Plantation Room is our main dining room and offers breakfast, lunch and dinner service, we also have a Library bar a great central gathering place, our Tiki bar is open seasonally and is well attended by guests and neighbors who can pull up their boat and enjoy our great culinary fare and the beautiful Florida sunshine.  Our Pro-Bar offers a great menu for those golfers who want a quick burger or our wonderful members who enjoy a great sandwich, cold beverage a perfect view of the golf course.

The resort rests on 232 acres of lush greens, emerald pines and grand oaks is manicured with great precision.  Our196 well appointed and spacious guest rooms and suites which include 12 two story golf villas with a spectacular view of the golf course offer the comfort of true hospitality and a tranquil experience.


Our Marina and Dive Shop offers great water activities, boat rentals, kayak rentals, canoe rentals, guided river tours, scuba diving tours, PADI certification and Manatee snorkel tours during the peak season from October to March,  we do have year round Manatee residence but recommend tours during peak winter months.  


The finest of Florida golf rave our golf enthusiasts who travel to conquer our Mark Mahannah designed 18 holes championship course; you can mix and match our three nines to suit your particular strength or weakness.  If it’s a short course you prefer, our 9 hole Lagoons course and is a great option to sharpen your short game.  Our links are beautifully manicured and well groomed; the course has a variety of water and bunker obstacles.  The course has aged well and offers an assortment of challenging fairways lined with mature emerald pines, grand oaks and is home to much wildlife.


Our full service Aveda Spa offers; hair, nail and skincare services as well as couples massage room with a working fireplace and a perfect setting for a romantic getaway or that honeymoon that you never took.


We have a lagoon style heated swimming pool and a Jacuzzi overlooking the beautiful river; we offer our guests food and beverage service from our Tiki bar which is open seasonally. 


The Plantation Room is our main dining room and offers breakfast, lunch and dinner service, we also have a Library bar a great central gathering place, our Tiki bar is open seasonally and is well attended by guests and neighbors who can pull up their boat and enjoy our great culinary fare and the beautiful Florida sunshine.  Our Pro-Bar offers a great menu for those golfers who want a quick burger or our wonderful members who enjoy a great sandwich, cold beverage a perfect view of the golf course.

title: Bonnet House Fine Artists Exhibitions
description: An extraordinary blend of art, architecture, history and ecology. This 35-acre subtropical estate and historic house museum was designed by Frederic Clay Bartlett, a noted painter and art collector. Bonnet House is one of the few complete homes and studios of two American artists with original furnishings open to the public. A nature trail walk taking up to 30 minutes is available. Guided golf cart tour of nature trail available. Outdoor rental space available.

Downtown DeLand is an award winning MainStreet community where we have learned to cherish that which is special about our past while still planning and moving into the 21st Century. MainStreet DeLand has many dedicated merchants and volunteers who work daily to maintain a lively and economically successful downtown.

We invite you to see for yourself what makes MainStreet DeLand so special. Spend a day downtown browsing our shops and galleries; dine at one of our great restaurants; have a coffee pick-me-up in one of our specialty coffee shops. You won't be disappointed!

title: Bonnet House Fine Artists Exhibitions
description: An extraordinary blend of art, architecture, history and ecology. This 35-acre subtropical estate and historic house museum was designed by Frederic Clay Bartlett, a noted painter and art collector. Bonnet House is one of the few complete homes and studios of two American artists with original furnishings open to the public. A nature trail walk taking up to 30 minutes is available. Guided golf cart tour of nature trail available. Outdoor rental space available.

title: Veterans Day Muster XVI
description: The only museum in the world dedicated exclusively to the elite warriors of Naval Special Warfare, Scouts and Raiders, OSS-MU, Naval Combat Demolition Units (NCDU), Underwater Demolition Teams (UDT) and SEAL Teams. Visit many outdoor exhibits on the site of the original Navy Frogman training grounds. Inside the museum are exhibits highlighting each conflict from WWII to the present. The museum theater presents Naval Special Warfare videos.

title: 21st Annual Holiday Open House
description:
Enjoy a complimentary tour and wine tasting at Florida's largest winery! A fun, interactive tour, leading up to the process of tasting wines is family friendly and lasts approximately 45 minutes to an hour.

After a brief video detailing the wine-making process, you will be guided through the bottling and fermentation area, lead onto a terrace overlooking acres of the vineyards and then downstairs to the tasting counter where you will enjoy a variety of Lakeridge wines.

title: St. Armands Fall Art Festival
description: St. Armands Circle is renowned as a continental marketplace, on a beautiful tropical island, and located only one block away from beautiful Lido Beach and the Gulf of Mexico. The Circle is a charming and graceful synthesis of past and present.  Relax and enjoy award winning restaurants, shop for trinkets and treasures, high fashion and home decor; from gourmet snacks to candleit fesats, you'll find it all on St. Armands Circle.  St. Armands Circle was the vision of circus magnate John Ringling, who purchased the island in 1917.  He planned a luxury development inclduing custom residences and upscale shopping on a roundabout.  In 1926, amidst pomp and ceremony, the John Ringling Causeway and the John Ringling Estates opened to the public.  Ringling's influence is evident today in the design of the streets radiating from the island's hud and the Italian Statuary from his personal collection.  There's always something happening on the Circle with our exciting special events calendar.  You'll find everything from art festivals to a wonderful family Halloween event to a romatic bridal event under the stars.  Plus there's a St. Armands-style Mardi Gras cekebration, spectacular cars shows featuring fabulous Ferrari's, Posh Porsche's, Jazz Jaguar's and Classic Corvettes - but the most magical night of all iis "Holiday Night of Lights" - our holiday season extravaganza!  Visit our website at www.starmandscircleassoc.com to stay in touch with all that is happening on the circle throughout the year.  Over 140 merchants on St. Armands Circle are committed to making your visit as memorable as it is rewarding.  Visit for a day or stay for a lifetime; the St. Armands experience is pne you won't soon forget.  You want have to travel far to find the world's treasures; they're all here on St. Armands Circle!

Downtown DeLand is an award winning MainStreet community where we have learned to cherish that which is special about our past while still planning and moving into the 21st Century. MainStreet DeLand has many dedicated merchants and volunteers who work daily to maintain a lively and economically successful downtown.

We invite you to see for yourself what makes MainStreet DeLand so special. Spend a day downtown browsing our shops and galleries; dine at one of our great restaurants; have a coffee pick-me-up in one of our specialty coffee shops. You won't be disappointed!

title: 4th Annual Bonnet House Orchid Fair
description: An extraordinary blend of art, architecture, history and ecology. This 35-acre subtropical estate and historic house museum was designed by Frederic Clay Bartlett, a noted painter and art collector. Bonnet House is one of the few complete homes and studios of two American artists with original furnishings open to the public. A nature trail walk taking up to 30 minutes is available. Guided golf cart tour of nature trail available. Outdoor rental space available.

title: Wine & Chocolate Festival
description:
Enjoy a complimentary tour and wine tasting at Florida's largest winery! A fun, interactive tour, leading up to the process of tasting wines is family friendly and lasts approximately 45 minutes to an hour.

After a brief video detailing the wine-making process, you will be guided through the bottling and fermentation area, lead onto a terrace overlooking acres of the vineyards and then downstairs to the tasting counter where you will enjoy a variety of Lakeridge wines.

title: 15th Annual Space Coast Birding & Wildlife Festival
description: The BNA is a  non-profit organization dedicated to protecting natural resources, raising awareness for sensible growth management through education and community-based strategic planning, providing cultural/heritage, conservation and environmental educational opportunities and supporting nature-based tourism in Brevard County. The BNA presents the Annual Space Coast Birding & Wildlife Festival.  The 15th Annual Festival is scheduled for January 25 through January 30, 2012. Festival activities feature unique birding, wildlife, nature, technology, cultural/historical and photography field trips, paddling adventures, Pelagic birding boat trip, classroom and evening keynote presentations as well as an Art Show & Competition and Nature-based Exhibits. Nationally recognized naturalists, scientists, biologists, photographers and ornithologists lead the Festival events and are available to participants for one-on-one discussions and instructions.

title: Behind the Science at Mote
description:
Ocean adventures await year ’round at Mote Aquarium, home to more than 100 marine species and exhibits showcasing the adjoining Mote Marine Laboratory. See freaky frogfish, huge scuttling lobsters and other denizens of Southwest Florida’s Gulf Coast, including sandbar, nurse, blacknose and bonnethead sharks. Guests can also see dolphins, manatees and sea turtles.

At our brand new exhibit, the Seahorse Conservation Laboratory, you can see graceful seahorses and their tiny young, or fry. You can learn about the threats wild seahorses face and watch Mote aquarists raise these fragile fish. Guests might even witness a little seahorse romance or spot a pregnant dad (that's right — male seahorses are the only animal dads that carry young in a belly pouch). 

At our new exhibit Sea Turtles: Ancient Survivors, visitors can learn how sea turtles outlived the dinosaurs and how these animals need our help to survive in modern times. An interactive display even lets you follow the journey of real sea turtles tagged in the wild by Mote scientists and see where they went between feeding and breeding seasons.

If you want to dive deeper into ocean fun, try our new "Breakfast at Mote" tours. These group tours allow small groups to enjoy Mote’s facilities before we open our doors to the general public. Participants can linger in front of their favorite exhibits, take unobstructed photos and even see bits of our morning routine, from fish feedings to shark tank cleanings. Your admission includes a continental breakfast and guided Aquarium tour. Ticket prices are $23 per person ($11 for Mote members). Go to www.mote.org/breakfast for more info.

When you buy a ticket to Mote Aquarium, you support world-renowned research at Mote Marine Laboratory. Visitors can glimpse our cutting-edge science and learn about the lab’s founding director, Eugenie Clark, and the research she did when the lab opened its doors in 1955. You can also see the work she and other researchers are doing at Mote today.

Mote Aquarium is open from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. 365 days a year at 1600 Ken Thompson Parkway, City Island, Sarasota. Admission prices are $17 for adults, $16 for seniors and $12 for kids ages 4-12. Mote Members and kids 3 and younger always get in free.

title: First Annual Spring into Fun
description:
A Place for Retreat and Renewal on Florida's Nature Coast

Experience 636 acres of natural Florida at Otter Springs Park & Campground.

Our centerpiece, Otter Springs, is a second magnitude natural spring with a constant temperature of 73 degrees and a flow of 10 million gallons of sparkling pure water daily. The spring creates a large clear pool and stream, which flows into the nearby Suwannee River.

The serene setting is perfect for fishing, bird watching, hiking, biking and other outdoor activities.  We have miles of trails in the park and are close to the Nature Coast State Trail.  Indoors at the Little Otter Club we offer a gym, board games, foosball, and cards.  We also have ladder golf, washer toss, croquet and horseshoes.

And when you want a little bit of both indoor comfort and outdoor beauty, relax at a poolside table or swim laps in our spacious, enclosed pool pavilion.

title: Hoedown at the Carriage Museum
description:
The Florida Carriage Museum & Resort encompasses over 400 acres of beauty in Central Florida’s horse country. Visitors to the Museum re-live history as they experience one of the finest collections of carriages in the world. They can even take a carriage ride (by prior appointment) on the winding roads through tall oaks draped in Spanish Moss, around the Qin Dynasty Gardens and past the exotic Japanese Koi Pond. Horses abound: a rare Poitou donkey named “Nicolette” and her best friend, a Miniature Horse named “Gracie”, welcome visitors and look for a scratch on the head.

The Museum houses one of the largest, privately owned collections of carriages in the world. It is open to the public and there are more than 160 meticulously restored carriages, including the 1840’s Dress Chariot formerly owned by Emperor Franz Joseph of Austria.

The Resort features 24 well appointed residences and 10 barns that serve as an equine “Bed & Barn.” Some guests bring their horses to train for the winter months, a weekend, or just for the day. Others come without horses to enjoy the miles of walking/carriage trails and can often be spotted picnicing under the shady oak trees.

Beautiful white-sand beaches lined with exotic seashells, breathtaking sunsets, tropical wildlife, nature preserves, history- and nature-based attractions and adventures for the entire family. title: Little Loggerhead Kids Program
description:
Sitting right on the ocean on Jupiter's majestic coastline. Elegant yet casual, tranquil yet exciting, this AAA Four-Diamond Palm Beach Florida resort boasts 168 beautifully appointed guestrooms and suites that provide comfort and style. Private balconies with spectacular ocean or sunset views are waiting for you.


Family packages, kids programs, and pet-friendly packages are featured at our resort for the best in fun for the entire family. Lounge outdoors in our all-new cozy seating with fire pit, and utilize the Spa, oceanfront pool and jacuzzi, and kids gameroom.  Affordable luxury awaits you.


Room amenities include down-filled duvets, feather pillows, lush terry robes, complimentary high-speed Internet access, flat panel TV and CD player. Dine in Sinclairs Ocean Grille or enjoy casual , fare from the Sandbar. Indulge at the resort's new full-service spa, and enjoy all the surrounding activities, shopping, dining and fun that awaits you in Jupiter, Florida.

title: Corporate Sail-Race Challenge
address: South Seas Island Resort - Captiva Island
city: Captiva Island and Ft Myers Beach FL
description:
Offshore Sailing School provides rewarding learning vacations at three premier SW Florida destination resorts. We give new meaning to fun-in-the-sun. Just want to try sailing? Learn how to make a boat move with wind alone? Pick any two days for a Learn to Sail or Learn to Cruise Adventure, or take a two-hour lesson. Gain Certification while you Learn to sail, cruise or race in three to five fun-filled days on the Gulf of Mexico or Tampa Bay.


Founded in 1964 by Olympic and America's Cup sailor, Steve Colgate, America's #1 Sailing School® also offers private and group lessons and sunset sails for vacationers already on site. Live aboard and shore based vacations include course and accommodations. Beginners and racers learn on award-winning Colgate 26 sailboats. Cruising courses are taught on state-of-the-art 43-49 foot cruising sailboats. Each day allows free time to enjoy other activities where you learn. Walk or drive Ding Darling National Refuge. Go to the Shell Museum. Fish, jog. bike, kayak, play tennis, enjoy a round of golf. Go shelling on long beautiful beaches, bask by gorgeous pools.    To learn more call 800-221-4326 or contact us on the web at  www.offshoresailing.com/contact.aspx  


Group and private programs available whether traveling alone, with a loved one, or the entire family. Private courses for two empower and build confidence. Singles make new friends while learning. These fun sailing adventures provide lasting skills and lifelong vacations under sail. As you sail and learn dolphins play in your wake and curious manatees circle as you dock.


Offshore Sailing School learning vacations and lessons are available at Pink Shell Beach Resort & Spa, Ft. Myers Beach; South Seas Island Resort, Captiva Island; and Mansion House B&B, St. Petersburg. Sailing is a green activity. It's fun and exhilarating to make a boat move with wind and sails alone. Reduce your carbon footprint every minute you're under sail. Sailing provides peace, freedom, inspiration and fun.


Call 800-221-4326 or contact us on the web at www.offshoresailing.com/contact.aspx


                                             Sailing—Good for You. Good for the World!(TM)

title: Possibilities in Pastel V
description:
For over 30 years, the Dunedin Fine Art Center (DFAC) has been offering exciting art opportunities in a most welcoming kind of way. St. Petersburg Times writer Lennie Bennett says that DFAC is “the artistic equivalent of a village square,” offering quality experiences to people of all ages. DFAC offers year-round exhibitions in four galleries featuring national, regional and local artists. Classes for students 4 yrs. to 94 yrs. fill 7 studio classrooms and a changing yearly theme makes the David L. Mason Children’s Art Museum a hands-on experience not to be missed.


You can take some time to enjoy a delicious lunch or gourmet coffee in the Palm Café, or search out one-of-a-kind gifts in the Gallery Gift Shop. Come out and PLAY at the Dunedin Fine Art Center and see why people say it’s where the ART is!

title: Road To Victory Museum
description:
"Florida as it was meant to be." No crowds, no lines, no parking meters, no high rises.
Located just north of Palm Beach International Airport and two hour drive from both Miami and Orlando.

Whether escaping from 50-hour work weeks, cold temperatures, or just the same old grind, come discover Startm Martin County, Florida and its surrounding ities to see what you have been missing. Catering to young and old alike, families, couples or groups, Martin County is your escape for antique hunting, renewing the spirit on a pristine beach, exploring the wonders of nature, or practicing your golf swing.Shopping in the historic downtowns and villages of Stuart, Jensen Beach, Hobe Sound and Port Salerno, offers a bouquet of boutiques, top-rated restaurants, art galleries and museums.

Families with children can escape to Martin County’s, one-of-a-kind marine center Florida Oceanographic Coastal Science Center to let the kids hand-feed sting rays, or take a river cruise to learn more about the Indian River Lagoon estuary, the largest ecosystem in North America boasting 800 species of fish. 
 
Naturalists will find miles of hiking trails, kayak adventures, and ocean Beaches. Here you will find no high-rise buildings and no crowds. Martin County has taken great care to preserve its natural beauty while offering some of the finest recreational activities in the state.

title: Road To Victory Museum
description:
"Florida as it was meant to be." No crowds, no lines, no parking meters, no high rises.
Located just north of Palm Beach International Airport and two hour drive from both Miami and Orlando.

Whether escaping from 50-hour work weeks, cold temperatures, or just the same old grind, come discover Startm Martin County, Florida and its surrounding ities to see what you have been missing. Catering to young and old alike, families, couples or groups, Martin County is your escape for antique hunting, renewing the spirit on a pristine beach, exploring the wonders of nature, or practicing your golf swing.Shopping in the historic downtowns and villages of Stuart, Jensen Beach, Hobe Sound and Port Salerno, offers a bouquet of boutiques, top-rated restaurants, art galleries and museums.

Families with children can escape to Martin County’s, one-of-a-kind marine center Florida Oceanographic Coastal Science Center to let the kids hand-feed sting rays, or take a river cruise to learn more about the Indian River Lagoon estuary, the largest ecosystem in North America boasting 800 species of fish. 
 
Naturalists will find miles of hiking trails, kayak adventures, and ocean Beaches. Here you will find no high-rise buildings and no crowds. Martin County has taken great care to preserve its natural beauty while offering some of the finest recreational activities in the state.

Become a part of the distinguished heritage of the AAA Four Diamond Casa Monica Hotel with a visit to this time-honored luxury boutique hotel, where the past and present seamlessly converge in a setting of regal beauty and inspired service.  Surrounded by original fine art, exquisite details and luxury amenities, the Casa Monica provides everything you desire for a truly memorable stay. 


Located in the heart of St. Augustine's historic downtown, the Casa Monica Hotel is conveniently situated within walking distance of the area's many popular historic attractions, museums, and shopping and dining opportunities, while award-wining golf courses and picturesque beaches are just minutes away.  Explore the charm of the nation's oldest city from the comfort of luxury accommodations reminiscent of times past.


The Casa Monica Hotel’s 138 luxurious guestrooms and suites reflect a romantic Spanish-style décor of wrought iron beds, mahogany furnishings, and subtle sea-toned fabrics. Pillowtop mattresses with triple sheeted bedding are topped with imported duvets to pamper and refresh.  Plush bathrobes, high speed wireless Internet, Bose CD radios, and other indulgent amenities make you wish you never have to leave.

title: Road To Victory Museum
description:
"Florida as it was meant to be." No crowds, no lines, no parking meters, no high rises.
Located just north of Palm Beach International Airport and two hour drive from both Miami and Orlando.

Whether escaping from 50-hour work weeks, cold temperatures, or just the same old grind, come discover Startm Martin County, Florida and its surrounding ities to see what you have been missing. Catering to young and old alike, families, couples or groups, Martin County is your escape for antique hunting, renewing the spirit on a pristine beach, exploring the wonders of nature, or practicing your golf swing.Shopping in the historic downtowns and villages of Stuart, Jensen Beach, Hobe Sound and Port Salerno, offers a bouquet of boutiques, top-rated restaurants, art galleries and museums.

Families with children can escape to Martin County’s, one-of-a-kind marine center Florida Oceanographic Coastal Science Center to let the kids hand-feed sting rays, or take a river cruise to learn more about the Indian River Lagoon estuary, the largest ecosystem in North America boasting 800 species of fish. 
 
Naturalists will find miles of hiking trails, kayak adventures, and ocean Beaches. Here you will find no high-rise buildings and no crowds. Martin County has taken great care to preserve its natural beauty while offering some of the finest recreational activities in the state.

title: Gator Nights Join In Tour
description:
One-of-a-kind airboat tour in the heart of the Florida Everglades. Come visit this family owned and operated classic South Florida attraction deep in the swamp. With a recent half-million dollar renovation, Sawgrass now offers two exclusive adventures, the daytime Private Tour and the nighttime Red Eye Tour! Feel the excitement and learn the history of Florida's most remarkable treasure, the Everglades. As one of the rare subtropical ecosystems, the Everglades holds spectacular mysteries.
     Renew your spirit as you glide across miles of river at speeds up to 40 mph and get up close and personal with native wildlife. This once in a lifetime adventure will create lasting memories as you discover the secrets of this untamed wilderness. Start your adventure with a 30 minute airboat tour of the Florida Everglades. Your tour will be guided by one of the experienced captains who have received extensive training.
     During the tour, you'll listen to tales of how the Seminole and panther once coexisted in this lush wilderness. Also, you'll catch a glimpse of endangered wildlife as you skim across the glassy water. Take a walk on the wild side back in time with an original dinosaur, the Florida Alligator. The reptile exhibit features dozens of species both native and exotic to Florida. Along with their friendly turtles and iguanas, you can learn about Cannibal, their 1,000-pound alligator. 
     Handlers are happy to demonstrate how these animals live and survive in the wild. Be sure to bring your camera, so you can capture the excitement of you cradling one of these majestic animals with the "Hold a Baby Alligator" experience. 
     Your adventure will include a visit to the Exotic Wildlife exhibit. Predators Unlimited is a separate organization that brings a variety of animals to the park each day to visit. They strive to educate and enlighten the public about endangered species like the Florida Panther. Playful critters abound and amaze as you can see many different animals that often include panthers, lepoards and wolves.
     While you are at Sawgrass please don't miss the "Swamp"yard Island! You and your family can interact and feed many of their animals at this exhibit.

title: Guided Hammock Walk
description: Gumbo Limbo Nature Centeris a distinctive part of the City of Boca Raton’s parks system.  The Center is surrounded by a rare remnant of coastal hammock, located on a barrier island.  A boardwalk provides access to this unique tropical forest where, from the 40-foot observation tower, you can view Gumbo Limbo trees, migrating birds, Indian middens, the ocean and the Intracoastal Waterway.  Outdoor seawater tanks house sea turtles, sharks and other marine life, while the Sea Turtle Rehabilitation Facility provides treatment and care for sick and injured sea turtles.  An informal garden attracts butterflies throughout the year.  Indoor displays feature wildlife indigenous to South Florida and a panorama of stained glass windows depicting the coastal island as it may have appeared in the 1500’s.  Florida Atlantic Universitymaintains an on-site marine biology research laboratory with a gallery above the lab allowing visitors to see projects conducted by university scientists.  Visit the gift shop for educational and fun nature books, toys, puzzles, t-shirts, jewelry and much more.

title: Behind the Science at Mote
description:
Ocean adventures await year ’round at Mote Aquarium, home to more than 100 marine species and exhibits showcasing the adjoining Mote Marine Laboratory. See freaky frogfish, huge scuttling lobsters and other denizens of Southwest Florida’s Gulf Coast, including sandbar, nurse, blacknose and bonnethead sharks. Guests can also see dolphins, manatees and sea turtles.

At our brand new exhibit, the Seahorse Conservation Laboratory, you can see graceful seahorses and their tiny young, or fry. You can learn about the threats wild seahorses face and watch Mote aquarists raise these fragile fish. Guests might even witness a little seahorse romance or spot a pregnant dad (that's right — male seahorses are the only animal dads that carry young in a belly pouch). 

At our new exhibit Sea Turtles: Ancient Survivors, visitors can learn how sea turtles outlived the dinosaurs and how these animals need our help to survive in modern times. An interactive display even lets you follow the journey of real sea turtles tagged in the wild by Mote scientists and see where they went between feeding and breeding seasons.

If you want to dive deeper into ocean fun, try our new "Breakfast at Mote" tours. These group tours allow small groups to enjoy Mote’s facilities before we open our doors to the general public. Participants can linger in front of their favorite exhibits, take unobstructed photos and even see bits of our morning routine, from fish feedings to shark tank cleanings. Your admission includes a continental breakfast and guided Aquarium tour. Ticket prices are $23 per person ($11 for Mote members). Go to www.mote.org/breakfast for more info.

When you buy a ticket to Mote Aquarium, you support world-renowned research at Mote Marine Laboratory. Visitors can glimpse our cutting-edge science and learn about the lab’s founding director, Eugenie Clark, and the research she did when the lab opened its doors in 1955. You can also see the work she and other researchers are doing at Mote today.

Mote Aquarium is open from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. 365 days a year at 1600 Ken Thompson Parkway, City Island, Sarasota. Admission prices are $17 for adults, $16 for seniors and $12 for kids ages 4-12. Mote Members and kids 3 and younger always get in free.

Welcome to the Hampton Inn & Suites-Homestead and all of South Florida’s famous fun, beauty and adventure. Easy to find, this Hampton Inn & Suites is located at the Florida Turnpike exit #2 and Campbell Drive in the historic town of Homestead, Florida. Founded as a turn-of-the-century destination, accessible via Henry Flagler’s Florida railway, Homestead has grown into one of the nation’s fastest growing cities while still retaining much of its quaint, small town atmosphere and friendly community spirit.

Bordered on the west by the wildly exotic Everglades National Park, the famous Florida Keys to the south and the cool blue of Biscayne Bay National Park to the east, this Hampton Inn & Suites is truly in one of the world’s most beautiful and vibrant locations.
